html:
Forehead and brow lift surgery are transformative procedures designed to rejuvenate the upper portion of your face, creating a more youthful and refreshed appearance. At AestheticEye in Cincinnati, OH, our board-certified oculoplastic surgeons, Dr. Ginger Henson and Dr. Jonathan Pargament, specialize in both traditional and endoscopic brow lifts. These advanced techniques help you achieve a natural, elevated look that enhances your overall facial harmony.

Why Consider a Forehead & Brow Lift?

As we age, the skin on our forehead and brows can begin to sag, leading to a tired or angry appearance. A forehead and brow lift can effectively address these concerns by lifting and tightening the skin and underlying tissues. Here are some benefits of the procedure:

Rejuvenated Appearance

Lifts sagging brows and smooths forehead wrinkles, giving you a more youthful look.

Improved Facial Harmony

Enhances the overall balance of your facial features.

Boosted Self-Confidence

A refreshed appearance can significantly boost your self-esteem.

Book An Appointment (937) 907-9009
Dr. Ginger Henson was a perfect choice for me! She did an excellent job. I had no pain and healed up better than ever! I’m so happy with the job she did for me!
Lynne S.

Traditional Brow Lift vs. Endoscopic Brow Lift

Traditional Brow Lift

A traditional brow lift involves making an incision along the hairline to lift and reposition the skin and underlying tissues. This method is particularly effective for individuals with significant sagging and deeper wrinkles.

Endoscopic Brow Lift in Cincinnati, OH

An endoscopic brow lift is a minimally invasive technique that uses small incisions and an endoscope (a tiny camera) to lift the brow. This method results in less scarring and a quicker recovery time while still providing excellent results.

View More Before & After Results

The Forehead & Brow Lift Procedure

At AestheticEye, our surgeons use advanced techniques to ensure optimal outcomes for both traditional and endoscopic brow lifts. The procedure involves:

  • Making incisions along the hairline or within the scalp.
  • Lifting and repositioning the underlying tissues and skin.
  • Removing excess skin and smoothing out wrinkles.
  • Closing the incisions with sutures or staples.

The choice between a traditional and endoscopic brow lift will depend on your specific needs and aesthetic goals, which will be thoroughly discussed during your consultation.

Book An Appointment (937) 907-9009

What to Expect in Recovery and Results

Recovery from a forehead and brow lift varies depending on the technique used. Generally, patients can expect:

Mild Swelling and Bruising

These symptoms typically subside within one to two weeks.

Minimal Discomfort

Pain is usually minimal and can be managed with prescribed medications.

Return to Normal Activities

Most patients return to their regular routines within 10-14 days.

The final results will become more apparent as swelling decreases, revealing a smoother, more youthful forehead and elevated brows.

Book An Appointment (937) 907-9009

Frequently Asked Questions | Forehead & Brow Lift Surgery

What Issues Can a Forehead & Brow Lift Address?

A forehead and brow lift can correct sagging brows, deep forehead wrinkles, and frown lines between the eyebrows, providing a more youthful and refreshed appearance.

Am I a Good Candidate for an Endoscopic Brow Lift?

Ideal candidates for an endoscopic brow lift are individuals with mild to moderate brow sagging who are looking for a minimally invasive option with quicker recovery times.

How Long Will the Results Last?

The results of a forehead and brow lift can last for many years, though the natural aging process will continue. Maintaining a healthy lifestyle and skincare routine can help prolong the results.

Are There Risks Associated with Brow Lift Surgery?

As with any surgical procedure, there are potential risks, including infection, scarring, and complications related to anesthesia. These risks are minimized when the surgery is performed by experienced oculoplastic surgeons like Dr. Henson and Dr. Pargament at AestheticEye.

What is the Difference Between a Traditional and Endoscopic Brow Lift?

A traditional brow lift involves a longer incision along the hairline and is ideal for significant sagging, while an endoscopic brow lift uses smaller incisions and a camera for a less invasive approach and quicker recovery.

How Soon Will I See Results After the Surgery?

Initial results can be seen as swelling and bruising subside, typically within two weeks. Full results, showcasing a smoother and more elevated brow area, will be visible in a few months.

Our expert surgeons, Dr. Henson and Dr. Pargament, are here to help you explore your options and develop a personalized treatment plan tailored to your needs. headings.title: Stye vs. Chalazion: Understanding the Difference

html:
Styes and chalazia are common eyelid conditions that can cause discomfort and affect the appearance of the eyes. At AestheticEye in Cincinnati, OH, our board-certified oculoplastic surgeons, Dr. Ginger Henson and Dr. Jonathan Pargament, specialize in the diagnosis and treatment of styes and chalazia, offering advanced solutions to alleviate symptoms and restore eyelid health. Serving Cincinnati, Dayton, our team is dedicated to providing personalized care for optimal results.

Stye vs. Chalazion: Understanding the Difference

What is a Stye?

A stye, or hordeolum, is an acute bacterial infection of the oil glands in the eyelid. It typically appears as a red, swollen, and painful lump near the edge of the eyelid. Styes can be external (on the outer part of the eyelid) or internal (inside the eyelid).

Book An Appointment (937) 907-9009
Dr. Ginger Henson was a perfect choice for me! She did an excellent job. I had no pain and healed up better than ever! I’m so happy with the job she did for me!
Lynne S.

What is a Chalazion?

A chalazion is a chronic, non-infectious blockage of the oil glands in the eyelid, resulting in a firm, painless lump. Unlike styes, chalazia usually develop further from the edge of the eyelid and are not associated with redness or acute pain.

Book An Appointment (937) 907-9009

Symptoms of Styes and Chalazia

Stye Symptoms

Redness and Swelling

A red, swollen bump on the eyelid, often near the lash line.

Pain or Tenderness

Discomfort, especially when touched.

Tearing

Excessive tearing from the affected eye.

Crusting

Crust formation along the eyelid margin.

Pus Discharge

Possible discharge from the stye.

Chalazion Symptoms

Painless Lump

A firm, non-tender lump further from the eyelid edge.

Mild Swelling

Swelling of the entire eyelid or just the affected area.

Blurry Vision

In some cases, pressure on the eyeball may cause temporary vision changes.

Cosmetic Concerns

Visible lump affecting the appearance of the eyelid.

Book An Appointment (937) 907-9009

What Causes Styes and Chalazia?

Causes of Styes

Styes are typically caused by bacterial infection, often Staphylococcus aureus, which infects the oil glands in the eyelid. Factors that increase the risk of developing a stye include:

Poor Eyelid Hygiene

Not cleaning the eyelids regularly.

Touching Eyes with Dirty Hands

Introducing bacteria to the eyelids.

Use of Expired or Contaminated Makeup

Bacteria from old makeup products.

Causes of Chalazia

Chalazia result from the blockage of oil glands (meibomian glands) in the eyelid. Contributing factors include:

Chronic Blepharitis

Inflammation of the eyelid margins.

Skin Conditions

Conditions such as rosacea or seborrheic dermatitis.

Previous Styes

Recurring styes can lead to the formation of chalazia.

Book An Appointment (937) 907-9009

Treatment Options for Styes and Chalazia in Cincinnati, OH

At AestheticEye, we offer comprehensive treatment options for styes and chalazia, tailored to each patient’s needs.

Non-Surgical Treatments

Warm Compresses

Applying warm compresses to the affected area several times a day to help reduce swelling and promote drainage.

Eyelid Hygiene

Keeping the eyelids clean with gentle cleansing solutions to prevent further infection or blockage.

Antibiotic Ointments or Drops

Prescribed for bacterial infections associated with styes.

Steroid Injections

For larger chalazia, to reduce inflammation and promote resolution.

Eyelid Chalazion Surgery

For persistent or recurrent chalazia that do not respond to non-surgical treatments, surgical intervention may be necessary. Our expert surgeons perform chalazion surgery with precision and care:

Incision and Drainage

A small incision is made on the inner side of the eyelid to drain the contents of the chalazion.

Local Anesthesia

The procedure is performed under local anesthesia to ensure patient comfort.

Quick Recovery

Most patients experience minimal discomfort and a quick recovery, returning to normal activities within a few days.

Book An Appointment (937) 907-9009

Frequently Asked Questions | Stye and Chalazion Drainage

How Can I Prevent Styes and Chalazia?

Maintaining good eyelid hygiene, avoiding touching your eyes with dirty hands, and using clean makeup products can help prevent styes and chalazia.

When Should I See a Doctor for a Stye or Chalazion?

You should see a doctor if you experience persistent or worsening symptoms, if the stye or chalazion does not improve with home treatments, or if it affects your vision.

Is Chalazion Surgery Painful?

Chalazion surgery is performed under local anesthesia, so patients do not feel pain during the procedure. Post-operative discomfort is usually minimal and can be managed with over-the-counter pain relievers.

Can Styes or Chalazia Recur After Treatment?

Yes, styes and chalazia can recur, especially if underlying risk factors are not addressed. Regular eyelid hygiene and preventive measures can help reduce the risk of recurrence.

How Long Does It Take to Recover from Chalazion Surgery?

Recovery from chalazion surgery is typically quick, with most patients resuming normal activities within a few days. Swelling and bruising may take a week or two to fully resolve.

Are There Any Risks Associated with Chalazion Surgery?

As with any surgical procedure, there are potential risks, including infection, bleeding, and scarring. These risks are minimized when the surgery is performed by experienced oculoplastic surgeons like Dr. Henson and Dr. Pargament at AestheticEye.

html:
Scarring on the eyelids can affect both the appearance and function of the eyes, causing discomfort and self-consciousness. At AestheticEye, our board-certified oculoplastic surgeons, Dr. Ginger Henson and Dr. Jonathan Pargament, specialize in advanced treatments for eyelid scar treatment and removal. We offer a range of non-surgical solutions designed to minimize scarring, improve skin texture, and restore confidence.

Understanding Eyelid Scarring

Eyelid scars can result from various causes, including trauma, surgery, infections, or inflammatory conditions. These scars can range from minor, barely noticeable marks to more significant scars that impact the appearance and function of the eyelids.

Common Causes of Eyelid Scarring

Trauma

Injuries or accidents that cause cuts or lacerations.

Surgery

Previous surgical procedures, including cosmetic or reconstructive surgeries.

Infections

Bacterial or viral infections leading to scarring.

Inflammatory Conditions

Chronic conditions such as blepharitis or dermatitis.

Impact of Eyelid Scars

Eyelid scars can cause a variety of issues, including:

Cosmetic Concerns

Visible scars can affect self-esteem and confidence.

Functional Issues

Scarring can impact eyelid movement and function, leading to discomfort or vision problems.

Skin Texture

Scars can cause uneven skin texture and pigmentation.

Advanced Non-Surgical Eyelid Scar Treatments in Cincinnati

At AestheticEye, we offer a variety of non-surgical treatments to address eyelid scars, providing effective solutions with minimal downtime. Our treatments are tailored to meet each patient’s unique needs, ensuring optimal results.

Book An Appointment (937) 907-9009

Laser Scar Removal

Laser therapy is an effective treatment for reducing the appearance of scars. This minimally invasive procedure uses focused light energy to break down scar tissue and stimulate collagen production, resulting in smoother, more even skin.

Benefits of Laser Scar Removal

Precision Treatment

Targets specific areas without damaging surrounding tissue.

Improves Texture and Tone

Reduces scar visibility and enhances skin texture.

Minimal Downtime

Most patients can resume normal activities shortly after treatment.

Book An Appointment (937) 907-9009

Microneedling

Microneedling involves using fine needles to create micro-injuries in the skin, stimulating the body’s natural healing process and promoting collagen and elastin production. This treatment can improve the appearance of scars and rejuvenate the skin.

Benefits of Microneedling

Enhanced Skin Renewal

Promotes the regeneration of healthy skin cells.

Reduces Scar Visibility

Effective for both new and old scars.

Quick Recovery

Minimal downtime with only mild redness and swelling.

Book An Appointment (937) 907-9009

Chemical Peels

Chemical peels use a specialized solution to exfoliate the top layers of skin, encouraging the growth of new, healthy skin cells. This treatment can improve skin texture, reduce pigmentation, and minimize the appearance of scars.

Benefits of Chemical Peels

Customized Treatments

Peels can be tailored to your skin type and concerns.

Smooths and Brightens

Improves overall skin tone and texture.

Non-Invasive

Requires little to no downtime for lighter peels.

Book An Appointment (937) 907-9009

Injectable Treatments

Injectable treatments, such as corticosteroids or other anti-inflammatory medications, can be used to reduce the appearance of raised scars. These injections can soften and flatten scars, improving their appearance and feel.

Benefits of Injectable Treatments

Targeted Action

Directly treats scar tissue to reduce its size and visibility.

Quick Procedure

Minimal discomfort and no downtime.

Effective for Hypertrophic Scars

Particularly useful for raised or thickened scars.

Book An Appointment (937) 907-9009

Topical Treatments

Topical treatments, including prescription creams and gels, can help reduce the appearance of scars over time. These treatments often contain ingredients like retinoids, silicone, or vitamin C to promote healing and improve skin texture.

Benefits of Topical Treatments

Easy Application

Simple to incorporate into your daily skincare routine.

Gradual Improvement

Noticeable results with consistent use.

Non-Invasive

No discomfort or downtime.

headings.title: Types of Neurotoxins We Offer at AestheticEye
Achieve a Smoother, Younger-Looking Appearance with Neurotoxins in Cincinnati, OH

html:
Neurotoxin injections are a popular and effective solution for reducing the appearance of fine lines and wrinkles, resulting in a smoother, more youthful complexion. These treatments work by temporarily relaxing the muscles responsible for causing dynamic wrinkles, such as crow’s feet, frown lines, and forehead creases. At AestheticEye in Cincinnati, we offer a range of neurotoxins to meet your aesthetic needs.

What Are Neurotoxins?

Neurotoxins are injectable treatments derived from botulinum toxin, which blocks nerve signals to the muscles, preventing them from contracting. This relaxation of the muscles leads to a reduction in the appearance of wrinkles and lines, providing a refreshed and rejuvenated look. Neurotoxin treatments are minimally invasive, involve little to no downtime, and deliver noticeable results within days.

html:
Dacryocystorhinostomy (DCR) surgery is a specialized procedure designed to treat blocked tear ducts, a condition that can cause excessive tearing, recurrent eye infections, and discomfort. At AestheticEye in Cincinnati, OH, our board-certified oculoplastic surgeons, Dr. Ginger Henson and Dr. Jonathan Pargament, offer advanced DCR surgery to help restore proper tear drainage and improve your eye health. Serving Cincinnati, Dayton, our team is committed to providing personalized care and effective solutions for blocked tear ducts.

Understanding Blocked Tear Ducts

A blocked tear duct occurs when the nasolacrimal duct, which drains tears from the eye into the nose, becomes obstructed. This can lead to excessive tearing (epiphora), recurrent eye infections, and inflammation. Blocked tear ducts can be congenital (present at birth) or acquired later in life due to injury, infection, or inflammation.

Book An Appointment (937) 907-9009
Dr. Ginger Henson was a perfect choice for me! She did an excellent job. I had no pain and healed up better than ever! I’m so happy with the job she did for me!
Lynne S.

Symptoms of Blocked Tear Ducts

Common symptoms of a blocked tear duct include:

Excessive Tearing

Persistent tearing that can cause blurred vision and discomfort.

Recurrent Eye Infections

Frequent infections due to stagnant tears providing a breeding ground for bacteria.

Swelling and Redness

Inflammation and redness around the inner corner of the eye.

Mucus Discharge

Discharge of mucus or pus from the eye, particularly when pressing on the area near the tear duct.

Book An Appointment (937) 907-9009

Causes of Blocked Tear Ducts

Blocked tear ducts can be caused by various factors, including:

Congenital Blockage

Incomplete development of the tear duct system at birth.

Infections

Chronic sinus infections or conjunctivitis that lead to scarring and blockage.

Trauma

Injury to the face or nose that damages the tear duct.

Inflammatory Conditions

Conditions such as sarcoidosis or Wegener’s granulomatosis that cause inflammation and blockage.

Book An Appointment (937) 907-9009

Dacryocystorhinostomy (DCR) Surgery

Dacryocystorhinostomy (DCR) surgery is a procedure that creates a new tear drainage pathway to bypass the blocked nasolacrimal duct. This allows tears to drain properly into the nose, alleviating the symptoms of a blocked tear duct.

Book An Appointment (937) 907-9009

Traditional DCR vs. Endoscopic DCR

There are two main approaches to DCR surgery:

Traditional (External) DCR

An incision is made on the side of the nose, near the inner corner of the eye. The surgeon creates a new drainage pathway from the lacrimal sac to the nasal cavity. This approach provides direct access to the tear drainage system and allows for precise reconstruction.

Endoscopic (Internal) DCR

Understanding Eye Removal Surgery: Enucleation vs. Evisceration

Eye removal surgery is sometimes necessary to treat severe eye conditions that cannot be managed with other treatments. There are two main types of eye removal surgery: enucleation and evisceration.

What is Enucleation?

Enucleation involves the complete removal of the eye, including the globe and part of the optic nerve. This procedure is typically performed to treat:

Ocular Tumors

Such as retinoblastoma or melanoma.

Severe Trauma

When the eye is irreparably damaged.

Infections

Chronic or severe infections that do not respond to treatment.

Painful Blind Eye

When a blind eye causes persistent pain.

Book An Appointment (937) 907-9009

What is Evisceration?

Evisceration involves the removal of the eye’s internal contents, leaving the scleral shell and extraocular muscles intact. This procedure is often chosen for:

Severe Infections

Where internal eye structures are infected.

Severe Trauma

When internal damage is extensive, but the outer eye structure is intact.

Blind Painful Eye

When the goal is to alleviate pain while preserving the eye’s external appearance.

Eye twitching, medically known as blepharospasm, can be a frustrating and disruptive condition. Characterized by involuntary muscle contractions around the eyes, blepharospasm can affect your daily life and overall well-being. At AestheticEye in Cincinnati, OH, our board-certified oculoplastic surgeons, Dr. Ginger Henson and Dr. Jonathan Pargament, specialize in diagnosing and treating blepharospasm to help you regain control and comfort.

Understanding Blepharospasm

Blepharospasm involves the involuntary twitching or spasms of the muscles around the eyes. This condition can range from mild, occasional twitching to severe, frequent spasms that can impact vision and quality of life. While the exact cause of blepharospasm is not always clear, it is often related to underlying neurological conditions, eye strain, or stress.

Dr. Ginger Henson was a perfect choice for me! She did an excellent job. I had no pain and healed up better than ever! I’m so happy with the job she did for me!
Lynne S.

Symptoms of Blepharospasm

Common symptoms of blepharospasm include:

Frequent Eye Twitching

Involuntary spasms of the eyelid muscles.

Difficulty Keeping Eyes Open

Severe cases may cause the eyelids to close involuntarily.

Increased Blinking

Frequent and uncontrollable blinking.

Eye Irritation

Discomfort and a sensation of dryness or grittiness in the eyes.

Light Sensitivity

Increased sensitivity to bright lights.

Book An Appointment (937) 907-9009

Causes of Eye Twitching

Blepharospasm can be triggered by various factors, including:

Neurological Disorders

Conditions such as dystonia or Parkinson’s disease.

Eye Strain

Prolonged use of digital screens or reading.

Stress and Fatigue

High levels of stress or lack of sleep.

Dry Eyes

Insufficient tear production leading to irritation.

Genetic Factors

Family history of blepharospasm.

Book An Appointment (937) 907-9009

Treatment Options for Blepharospasm

At AestheticEye, we offer a range of treatment options to manage and alleviate the symptoms of blepharospasm. Our goal is to improve your quality of life by reducing the frequency and severity of eye twitching.

Book An Appointment (937) 907-9009

Medical Treatments

Botox Injections

Botulinum toxin (Botox) injections are a common and effective treatment for blepharospasm. Botox temporarily paralyzes the muscles around the eyes, reducing involuntary twitching.

Medications

Certain medications can help manage symptoms by affecting the neurotransmitters involved in muscle contractions.

Surgical Treatments

In severe cases, surgical intervention may be necessary:

Myectomy

This procedure involves removing some of the muscles and nerves responsible for the twitching, providing long-term relief for severe blepharospasm.

Non-Surgical Options

Stress Management

Techniques such as relaxation exercises, meditation, and proper sleep can help reduce stress-induced twitching.

Eye Care

Regular use of lubricating eye drops can alleviate dryness and irritation, reducing the frequency of twitching.

Frequently Asked Questions | Blepharospasm Treatment

What Are the Early Signs of Blepharospasm?

Early signs include frequent, involuntary twitching of the eyelids and increased blinking. If left untreated, these symptoms can become more severe and disruptive.

Can Lifestyle Changes Help Manage Blepharospasm?

Yes, managing stress through relaxation techniques and ensuring adequate sleep can help reduce the frequency of eye twitching. Regular use of lubricating eye drops can also alleviate symptoms.

How Effective Are Botox Injections for Treating Eye Twitching?

Botox injections are highly effective for many patients, providing significant relief from involuntary muscle contractions around the eyes. The effects typically last for several months.

Is Surgery Always Necessary for Blepharospasm?

Surgery is usually considered only for severe cases that do not respond to other treatments. Many patients find relief through less invasive methods such as Botox injections and medications.

As with any medical treatment, there are potential risks, including infection, bruising, and temporary side effects from Botox injections. Our experienced oculoplastic surgeons at AestheticEye will discuss these risks with you and ensure you receive the safest and most effective treatment.

How Soon Can I Expect Results After Treatment?

Results from Botox injections can usually be seen within a few days to a week, while the benefits of surgical treatment may take longer to fully manifest as you heal.

Understanding Eyelid Malposition

Eyelid malposition can manifest in various forms, including ptosis (drooping eyelid), ectropion (outward turning eyelid), entropion (inward turning eyelid), and retraction (pulled back eyelid). Each condition presents unique challenges and can lead to discomfort, irritation, and even vision problems if left untreated.

Types of Eyelid Malposition

Ptosis (Drooping Eyelid)

Ptosis occurs when the upper eyelid droops over the eye, potentially obstructing vision. It can result from aging, muscle weakness, or neurological conditions.

Ectropion (Outward Turning Eyelid)

Ectropion is a condition where the lower eyelid turns outward, exposing the inner eyelid and causing irritation, excessive tearing, and increased risk of infection.

Entropion (Inward Turning Eyelid)

Entropion involves the inward turning of the eyelid, causing the eyelashes and skin to rub against the eye. This can lead to significant discomfort, irritation, and corneal damage.

Eyelid Retraction (Pulled Back Eyelid)

Eyelid retraction is when the eyelid is pulled back from its normal position, often due to thyroid eye disease or previous surgeries. This condition can result in dry eyes, irritation, and an altered appearance.

Facial paralysis and Bell’s palsy can have a significant impact on both appearance and function, affecting facial expressions, speech, and even eating. At AestheticEye in Cincinnati, OH, our board-certified oculoplastic surgeons, Dr. Ginger Henson and Dr. Jonathan Pargament, specialize in the diagnosis and treatment of facial paralysis and Bell’s palsy, offering comprehensive care and advanced nerve damage treatments to help restore function and improve quality of life.

Understanding Facial Paralysis and Bell’s Palsy

Facial paralysis occurs when the facial nerve, responsible for controlling the muscles of facial expression, is damaged. This can result from various causes, including trauma, infections, tumors, or neurological conditions. Bell’s palsy is a specific type of facial paralysis that typically presents as sudden, unilateral facial weakness or paralysis, often without a known cause.

Symptoms of Bell’s Palsy

The symptoms of facial paralysis and Bell’s palsy can vary but commonly include:

Sudden Weakness or Paralysis

Typically on one side of the face.

Drooping of the Mouth

Difficulty smiling or closing the mouth.

Inability to Close the Eye

Leading to dryness and irritation.

Loss of Facial Expression

Difficulty making facial expressions or movements.

Drooling and Difficulty Eating

Challenges with chewing and swallowing.

Changes in Tear and Saliva Production

Increased or decreased production.

Causes of Facial Paralysis

Facial paralysis can result from various conditions, including:

Bell's Palsy

Sudden, unexplained facial paralysis, often temporary.

Trauma

Injury to the facial nerve from accidents or surgeries.

Infections

Viral infections like herpes simplex virus.

Tumors

Growths affecting the facial nerve.

Neurological Conditions

Disorders such as stroke or multiple sclerosis.

Advanced Treatments for Facial Paralysis

At AestheticEye, we offer a range of treatments to address facial paralysis and Bell’s palsy, tailored to each patient’s specific condition and needs. Our goal is to restore function, improve appearance, and enhance overall quality of life.

Nerve Damage Treatment

Effective management of facial paralysis often involves treating the underlying nerve damage. Treatment options may include:

Medications

Anti-inflammatory or antiviral medications to reduce inflammation and treat infections.

Physical Therapy

Exercises and techniques to strengthen facial muscles and improve coordination.

Surgical Intervention

Procedures to repair or graft damaged nerves, restore muscle function, and improve symmetry.

Eyelid and Facial Surgery

In cases where facial paralysis affects the eyelids and surrounding structures, surgical intervention may be necessary to restore function and appearance:

Eyelid Weight Implants

Small weights implanted in the upper eyelid to help with closing the eye.

Gold or Platinum Weight Surgery

Weights are placed in the upper eyelid to aid in blinking and eye closure.

Facial Reanimation Surgery

Procedures to restore movement to the face by transferring nerves or muscles from other parts of the body.

Brow Lift and Eyelid Surgery

Procedures to correct drooping brows and sagging eyelids, improving facial symmetry and function.

Frequently Asked Questions | Facial Paralysis and Bell’s Palsy

Can Stress Trigger Bell’s Palsy?

While the exact cause of Bell’s palsy is unknown, stress is believed to be a contributing factor that can trigger the onset of the condition in some individuals.

Are There Non-Surgical Treatments for Facial Paralysis?

Yes, non-surgical treatments include medications to reduce inflammation or treat infections, physical therapy to strengthen facial muscles, and techniques to improve coordination and facial symmetry.

How Does Physical Therapy Help with Facial Paralysis?

Physical therapy can help retrain facial muscles, improve muscle strength, and enhance coordination, which can lead to improved facial movements and expressions.

What Is Facial Reanimation Surgery?

Facial reanimation surgery involves procedures to restore movement to the paralyzed areas of the face. This can include nerve grafts, muscle transfers, and other techniques to enhance facial symmetry and function.

Can Bell’s Palsy Recur?

While rare, Bell’s palsy can recur in some individuals, either on the same side or the opposite side of the face. Regular follow-ups and managing underlying risk factors can help reduce the chances of recurrence.

How Soon Should I Seek Treatment for Bell’s Palsy?

It is important to seek medical attention as soon as possible after noticing symptoms of Bell’s palsy. Early intervention with medications can improve the chances of a full recovery.

Is It Possible to Prevent Facial Paralysis?

Preventing facial paralysis involves managing risk factors such as controlling infections, protecting the face from trauma, and addressing underlying health conditions that could contribute to nerve damage.

Orbital decompression surgery is a specialized procedure designed to relieve pressure within the orbit (eye socket) and create more space for the eye. At AestheticEye in Cincinnati, OH, our board-certified oculoplastic surgeons, Dr. Ginger Henson and Dr. Jonathan Pargament, are experts in performing this delicate surgery. Serving patients in Cincinnati, Dayton, our team is dedicated to providing advanced surgical solutions with a focus on patient care and exceptional results.

What is Orbital Decompression Surgery?

Orbital decompression surgery is primarily used to treat conditions that cause the tissues within the eye socket to become inflamed and swollen, leading to increased pressure. This procedure involves removing or reshaping parts of the bone and sometimes removing fat from the orbit to reduce pressure and allow the eye to return to its normal position.

Conditions We Treat with Orbital Decompression

The most common condition treated with orbital decompression surgery is thyroid eye disease (TED), also known as Graves’ orbitopathy. This autoimmune disorder causes the tissues around the eyes to swell, resulting in:

Proptosis (Bulging Eyes)

Eyes that appear to protrude from the eye sockets.

Eyelid Retraction

Eyelids that are pulled back, exposing more of the eye.

Double Vision

Misalignment of the eyes leading to seeing double.

Eye Pain and Discomfort

Due to increased pressure and inflammation.

Vision Problems

Severe cases can lead to vision impairment or loss if the optic nerve is compressed.

Who Needs Orbital Decompression Surgery?

Orbital decompression surgery is recommended for individuals with thyroid eye disease or other conditions that cause significant eye bulging and pressure, leading to discomfort or vision issues. Candidates for this surgery typically include those who:

Have Severe Proptosis

Eyes that are noticeably bulging and causing cosmetic concerns or functional issues.

Experience Pain and Discomfort

Persistent pain or discomfort in the eye area due to increased pressure.

Suffer from Vision Problems

Vision impairment or risk of vision loss due to optic nerve compression.

Are Unresponsive to Other Treatments

Have not found relief from other medical treatments, such as medications or non-surgical interventions.

Bone Removal

Removing or reshaping parts of the orbital bones to create more space within the eye socket.

In some cases, excess fat is removed to further reduce pressure and allow the eye to settle back into a more natural position.

The procedure usually takes a few hours, depending on the complexity of the case.

Eye Tear Duct Surgery: Dacryocystorhinostomy (DCR)

Dacryocystorhinostomy (DCR) is a common surgical procedure used to treat blocked tear ducts. This procedure creates a new tear drainage pathway to bypass the blockage, allowing tears to drain properly into the nasal cavity.

The DCR Procedure

Incision

A small incision is made near the inner corner of the eye or inside the nose to access the tear duct.

New Drainage Pathway

A new pathway is created between the lacrimal sac and the nasal cavity to allow tears to drain freely.

Stenting

In some cases, a tiny stent may be placed to keep the new drainage pathway open during healing.

Canaliculoplasty is a surgical procedure to widen the tear ducts if they are too narrow, ensuring better tear drainage.

Incision

A small incision is made in the tear duct.

Dilation

The duct is widened using specialized instruments.

Stenting

A stent may be placed to maintain the duct’s new width during healing.

Thyroid Eye Disease (TED), also known as Graves’ orbitopathy, is a complex condition that affects the tissues around the eyes, causing inflammation, swelling, and discomfort. At AestheticEye, our top oculoplastic surgeons in Cincinnati, Dr. Ginger Henson and Dr. Jonathan Pargament, specialize in the diagnosis and surgical treatment of TED. What is Thyroid Eye Disease?

Thyroid Eye Disease is an autoimmune disorder often associated with hyperthyroidism, where the body’s immune system attacks the tissues around the eyes. This results in inflammation and swelling, leading to a range of symptoms that can significantly impact your quality of life.

Symptoms of Thyroid Eye Disease

Common symptoms of TED include:

Proptosis (Bulging Eyes)

Eyes that appear to protrude from the eye sockets.

Eyelid Retraction

Eyelids that are pulled back, exposing more of the eye.

Double Vision

: Seeing double due to misalignment of the eyes.

Eye Pain and Discomfort

Persistent pain or discomfort around the eyes.

Dryness and Redness

Irritation and dryness caused by the exposure of the eye surface.

Vision Problems

Blurred vision or vision loss in severe cases.

Causes and Risk Factors of TED

Thyroid Eye Disease is most commonly associated with Graves’ disease, an autoimmune condition that affects the thyroid gland. Risk factors for TED include:

Hyperthyroidism

Overactive thyroid gland.

Smoking

Increases the severity of TED.

Gender

Women are more commonly affected than men.

Genetic Factors

Family history of thyroid or autoimmune diseases.

What Are the First Signs of Thyroid Eye Disease?

The initial signs of TED often include redness, swelling, and discomfort around the eyes. Patients may also notice bulging eyes and eyelid retraction.

How Long Does It Take to Recover from Orbital Decompression Surgery?

Recovery time varies, but most patients experience significant improvement within a few weeks. Full recovery may take several months, with regular follow-up appointments to monitor progress.

Can Thyroid Eye Disease Be Treated Without Surgery?

Mild cases of TED can often be managed with medications and lifestyle changes, such as quitting smoking. However, severe cases typically require surgical intervention for optimal outcomes.

Will My Vision Improve After Surgery for Thyroid Eye Disease?

Surgical treatment aims to alleviate symptoms and improve eye function. Many patients experience significant improvement in vision and relief from discomfort after surgery.

title: Pigmented Lesion Pre and Post Care Instructions
description: Understand the essential steps before and after pigmented lesion treatments to support safe healing and the best cosmetic outcomes.
html:
The following instructions are for laser and intense pulsed light (collectively referred to as laser) treatments for benign pigmented lesions.

PRE-TREATMENT INSTRUCTIONS

  • Avoid tanning bed, direct sun exposure, and sunless tanning products for 4 weeks prior to each treatment and the duration of treatments.
  • Use a broad-spectrum sunscreen of SPF 30 containing zinc oxide or titanium dioxide daily for the duration of treatments.
  • Do not use medications that cause photosensitivity (such as doxycycline and minocycline for at least 72 hours prior to each treatment).
  • If you have a history of herpes (oral cold sores, genital) or shingles in the treatment area, start your antiviral medication (valacyclovir, acyclovir) as directed for 2 days prior to treatment and continue for 3 days after treatment.
  • Discontinue use of glycolic and Retin-A containing products 1 week before treatments.
  • At the time of treatment, the area must be free of any open sores, lesions, or skin infections (e.g. active acne).

POST-TREATMENT INSTRUCTIONS

  • Immediately after treatment, pigmented lesions will appear darkened. The lesions will continue to darken and flake off over 1-2 weeks.
  • Some skin redness and swelling along with a mild to moderate sunburn sensation in the treatment area are common. This typically resolves within a few hours but may last up to 3 days.
  • Apply a wrapped cool compress or wrapped ice pack to the treated areas for 15 minutes every 1-2 hours as needed to reduce these symptoms. You may also apply hydrocortisone 1% over-the-counter cream two times per day on intact skin for up to 3 days to decrease any skin irritation.
  • Gently wash twice daily with mild soap, do not rub the skin vigorously and avoid hot water, as the skin will be fragile for several days.
  • Avoid activities that can cause flushing for 24 hours after treatment or until any swelling resolves.
  • Avoid any topical products that may cause irritation for 1 week following treatment.
  • Layer antibiotic ointment (such as bacitracin) to the area twice a day until the skin heals. Do not pick or attempt to remove scabs that form following your treatment, as this may incur infection or scarring.

html:
Mental & Emotional Well-Being in Your Recovery

We appreciate your trust in us and are honored to be part of your journey toward improved health and confidence. To ensure the best possible outcome, we’ve created this guide to help you prepare for your procedure and navigate your recovery with confidence. Please take the time to read through it carefully, as your active participation is a key factor in a smooth and successful healing process.

Surgery & Recovery Are a Team Effort

Think of your surgery and recovery as a partnership. You are not alone in this process—we are here to guide, support, and care for you. However, your role as a patient is just as essential as ours as your medical team. Carefully following pre- and post-operative instructions, attending scheduled follow-ups, and maintaining open and honest communication with us will help prevent complications and optimize your results. If you ever have concerns or questions, trust that we are here to assist you. Your commitment to this process will make all the difference.

The Power of a Positive Mindset

Your mental and emotional well-being play a significant role in your physical recovery. It’s normal to experience discomfort, swelling, or temporary changes in your appearance after surgery, but approaching this phase with a positive and patient mindset can make a remarkable difference. Focusing on healing, staying engaged in light activities when appropriate, and reminding yourself that recovery is a journey will help you manage the temporary challenges that come with it. Surround yourself with a supportive environment, and remember that each day brings progress, even if it doesn’t always feel that way.

Setting Realistic Expectations

It’s important to understand that the healing process varies for each patient, and results take time to fully develop. Initially, you may notice swelling, bruising, or asymmetry, which can be concerning if you’re not expecting it. This is a natural part of healing, and in most cases, things may appear worse before they improve. Patience is essential, as your body needs time to settle, adjust, and reveal the final outcome. Trust the process, and rest assured that we will be here to monitor your progress every step of the way

title: Pre-Operative Instructions – General
description: Ensure a smooth cosmetic surgery experience with our general pre-operative instructions. Learn what to do before your procedure for the best results.
html:
The following instructions should be followed closely except when overruled by specific procedural instructions:

TWO WEEKS PRIOR TO SURGERY

  • NO ASPRIN or medicines that contain aspirin as it interferes with normal blood clotting.
  • NO NSAIDS (Motrin, Advil, Aleve) as it interferes with blood clotting
  • You MAY take Tylenol or generic forms of this drug.
  • AVOID vitamins and supplements
  • NO SMOKING. Nicotine reduces blood flow to the skin and can cause complications during your recovery.

ONE WEEK PRIOR TO SURGERY

  • DO NOT drink alcohol or take any illicit substances for 24 hours prior as these can interfere with anesthesia and affect blood clotting.
  • DO NOT take any cough or cold medications without permission. Be sure to report any sights of cold, infection, boils or pustules appearing before surgery.
  • ARRANGE FOR a responsible adult to drive you to and from the facility on the day of surgery. You will not be able to leave on your own nor will a cab or bus driver be allowed to take you home from surgery.
  • ARRANGE FOR a responsible adult to spend the first 24 hours with you. You cannot be left alone directly after surgery.
  • If you’re on regular medications, please clear these with the prescribing doctor.

NIGHT BEFORE & MORNING OF SURGERY

  • DO NOT eat or drink anything – including water – after midnight the night before your surgery. No gum, candy, mints or coffee the morning of surgery.
  • DO NOT apply any of the following on your skin, hair or face the morning of surgery:
    • Makeup
    • Creams/Lotions
    • Hair Gels or Spray
    • Perfumes
    • Powders
    • Deodarant
  • You may brush your teeth, but do not drink anything
  • DO NOT wear your contacts to surgery. If you wear glasses, bring your glasses case.
  • Wear comfortable, loose-fitting clothes that do not have to be put on over your head. We suggest a button-up top and pull on pants. You will want shoes that are easy to slip on.
  • Do NOT bring any valuables or wear any jewelry. All facial and body piercings must be removed.
  • BRING ALL medications and supplements with you the day of surgery and to all post-operative visits.

title: Dermal Filler Pre & Post Care Instructions
description: Discover essential pre- and post-care instructions for dermal fillers to ensure smooth recovery and optimal results at Aesthetic Eye in Cincinnati, OH.
html:
PRE-TREATMENT INSTRUCTIONS

  • Avoid anti-inflammatory/blood thinning medications, if possible for a period of 2 weeks before treatment. Medications and supplements such as aspirin, vitamin E, ginkgo biloba, ginseng, St. John’s Wort, Omega 3/Fish Oil supplements, Ibuprofen, Motrin, Advil, Aleve and other NSAIDS have a blood thinning effect and can increase the risk of bruising and swelling after injections
  • You are not a candidate if you are pregnant or breastfeeding.

POST-TREATMENT INSTRUCTIONS

  • Avoid significant movement of the treated area. Unless instructed by the provider.
  • Avoid strenuous exercise for 24 hours.
  • Avoid extensive sun or heat for 72 hours.
  • Avoid consuming excess amounts of alcohol or salts to avoid excess swelling.
  • If you have swelling you may apply a cool compress for 15 minutes each hour.
  • Use Tylenol for discomfort.
  • If you experience swelling, try to sleep face up and slightly elevated.

title: HydraFacial Pre & Post Care Instructions
description: Discover essential pre- and post-care instructions for HydraFacial treatments at Aesthetic Eye in Cincinnati, OH. Ensure optimal results and smooth recovery with expert guidance.
html:
PRE-TREATMENT INSTRUCTIONS

  • Avoid excess sun exposure, including tanning beds for 1 week before treatment
  • Do not use any type of exfoliants 2 days before treatment.
  • Refrain from any chemical peels or lasers for 2 weeks prior.
  • Discontinue use of Tretinoin type products (Renova, Tretinoin, Retin A, Retin A Micro, Tri-Luma, Solage, etc.) at least 2 days before treatment.
  • Discontinue use of Hydroquinone 2-3 days before treatment.
  • If you have a history of cold sores, consider beginning prophylactic treatment with Valtrex or similar no later than the day of treatment.
  • Wait 2 weeks after Botox and filler treatments to have a HydraFacial treatment.
  • Botox and filler may be done on the same day, but only after HydraFacial treatment.

POST-TREATMENT INSTRUCTIONS

  • Avoid any exfoliation to the area for 48 hours post-treatment.
  • To keep the area clean, avoid heat sources, including hot showers, saunas, and cardio workouts that may produce sweat for 24 hours.
  • You may wash your face the following morning.
  • Do not use topical Retin-A for 2 days following treatment.
  • Avoid unprotected sun exposure and/or use of tanning beds for at least 3 days post-treatment.
  • Use sunscreen with SPF 30 or higher daily for 3-5 days post-treatment.
  • Makeup may be applied the day after treatment.

  • Don’t bend down. Avoid things like yoga or bending over for long periods of time.
  • It can take approximately 4 to 7 days for results to be seen. If the desired result is not seen after 2 weeks of your treatment you may need additional Botox.
  • Do NOT perform activities involving straining, heavy lifting, or vigorous exercise for 12 hours after treatment. This will keep the Botox in the intended area it was injected into.

title: Chemical Peel Pre & Post Treatment Care Instructions
description: Discover pre- and post-treatment care instructions for chemical peels to ensure optimal results and recovery at Aesthetic Eye MD.
html:
PRE-TREATMENT CARE INSTRUCTIONS

  • Stop topical acne regimen such as Retin-A, Tretinoin, Adapalene, Benzoyl Peroxide, Salicylic Acid 5 days prior to your peel.
  • If you have been on Accutane within the past 6 months you should not have a peel.

POST-TREATMENT INSTRUCTIONS

  • Redness and sensitivity might be present (and last up to a few days).
  • Do NOT wash your face.
  • Treat skin gently by washing with a gentle cleanser, cool water, using hands only, pat dry
    and immediately apply a gentle moisturizer.
  • No exercising or activities that cause excessive sweating.
  • Avoid showers or wetting your face
  • Avoid sun tanning and prolonged exposure to direct sunlight.
  • When exposed to sun, always use sunscreen SPF 30 or above.
  • Do not apply anything except approved products to your skin.
  • Peeling will begin 36-48 hours after peel (and last anywhere from 3-7 days).
  • Peeling can be similar to that of a sunburn or light flaking.
  • Do NOT pick or prematurely peel the skin.
  • May use mineral makeup after 12 hours but it is not recommended while you are peeling.
  • Repeat treatments in 4 weeks and for best results complete a series of 3 – 5 treatments.

title: Dermaplaning Pre & Post Care Instructions

title: SkinPen Microneedling Pre & Post Care Instructions
description: Learn pre- and post-care instructions for SkinPen microneedling at Aesthetic Eye in Cincinnati, OH. Follow expert guidelines for optimal results and smooth recovery.
html:
PRE-TREATMENT INSTRUCTIONS

  • Avoidance of Accutane for the past 6 months.
  • Avoidance of retinoids, topical acne medications, exfoliants, hydroquinone, and benzoyl peroxide 5 days prior to procedure.
  • Avoidance of chemical peels, IPL or other Laser procedures for at least 1 week prior treatment and post treatment.
  • No waxing, depilatory creams or electrolysis 5-7 days prior.
  • No significant changes in the skin recently reported including breakdown of skin or excess dryness or sunburn

DAY OF PROCEDURE

  • No lotions, makeup or other topical products should be on your face before your procedure.
  • Please arrive with clean washed skin, but if this is not possible, we will cleanse it for you.
  • After your procedure your medical provider may apply a healing cream and sunscreen.
  • You may clean your face with a gentle cleanser before bed.

POST-TREATMENT INSTRUCTIONS

  • Redness or sensitivity might be present and can last up to a few days. Continue to use recommended skincare as instructed.
  • Avoid sun tanning and prolonged exposure to direct sunlight.
  • When exposed to sun, always use an approved sunscreen of SPF 30 or above.
  • Use Tylenol only as needed for any soreness.
  • Avoid strenuous exercise or sweating for 12 hours after the procedure.
  • Treat skin gently by washing with a gentle cleanser, cool water, using hands only and pat dry no earlier than 4
    hours after.
  • Avoid makeup for 24 hours post procedure. You may use mineral makeup after 24 hours.
  • Repeat treatments in 4 weeks and for best results complete a series of 3 – 5 treatments.
  • Immediately after your Micro-Needling procedure, do not take any anti-inflammatory medications such as Ibuprofen, Motrin or Advil. These agents will interfere with the natural inflammatory process that is critical and responsible for your skin rejuvenation.

title: 3DMIRACL Non-Ablative Laser Resurfacing Pre & Post Care Instructions
description: Get the best results from your 3DMIRACL laser resurfacing at AestheticEye. Follow these essential pre and post care tips to reduce discomfort, protect your skin, and enhance healing.
html:
Congratulations! You have made the decision to rejuvenate your skin with laser resurfacing! To achieve the best possible results and protect your skin, please carefully read and follow the instructions below.

WHAT TO EXPECT

  • Immediately after treatment, you will experience redness and moderate discomfort.
  • Heat sensation can be intense for the first 2-3 hours. It is normal to have discomfort similar to a significant sunburn for the first few days.
  • Swelling is expected, and usually worse in the morning. Swelling can be significant and cause a tight sensation to the skin
  • Pinpoint bleeding is possible for the first few days
  • Itching
  • Your skin may feel dry or flaky.
  • The skin will remain pink for some time after the treatment, for days to weeks.

PRE-TREATMENT INSTRUCTIONS

  • Discontinue skin irritants 1 week prior to your treatment (retinoids, salicylic acid, hydroquinone, glycolics, etc.)
  • Do not use medications that cause photosensitivity (doxycycline, minocycline for at least 3 days prior to your procedure).
  • Avoid sun exposure, tanning bed or sunless tanning products and use a broad spectrum sunscreen of SPF 30 or greater for the month prior to treatment.
  • Avoid deep facial peels for one month prior to treatment (this includes microdermabrasion, laser resurfacing or aggressive chemical peels)
  • Arrive on the day of the procedure with clean skin, free of makeup
  • Let us know if you are prone to cold sores or use a C-Pap while sleeping.

DAY OF TREATMENT: POST-TREATMENT INSTRUCTIONS

  • Immediately post treatment, a sunburn-like feeling is common. This can last up to a few hours post treatment. To reduce the discomfort and remove the heat, saline soaks are recommended.
  • Soak gauze in saline or sterile water and apply to the area that was treated. Keep the gauze on skin which will allow the skin to cool down for 5-10 minutes. Apply an occlusive moisturizer to keep the skin hydrated and protected.
  • Patients should sleep in a modified upright position along with a clean pillow case and linens the first night.

POST-TREATMENT SKIN CARE INSTRUCTIONS DAY 1

Next day use a gentle cleanser and moisturizer. Remove previous application of moisturizer with cool moist cloth prior to re-applying moisturizer. Repeat as often as needed for comfort.

POST-TREATMENT SKIN CARE INSTRUCTIONS DAY 2-7

Begin cleansing the treated areas with a gentle facial cleanser using nothing more abrasive than the fingertips. Do no scrub treated areas. Continue to apply moisturizer and SPF as needed. Patient should sleep in a modified upright position for the second night if needed.

title: UltraClear Ablative Laser Resurfacing Pre and Post Care Instructions
description: Get the most out of your UltraClear ablative laser resurfacing at AestheticEye. Follow detailed pre and post care instructions to manage redness, minimize peeling, and support skin renewal.
html:
Congratulations! You have made the decision to rejuvenate your skin with laser resurfacing! To achieve the best possible results and protect your skin, please carefully read and follow the instructions below.

WHAT TO EXPECT

  • Immediately after treatment, you will experience redness and moderate discomfort.
  • Heat sensation can be intense for the first 2-3 hours. It is normal to have discomfort similar to a significant sunburn for the first few days.
  • Swelling is expected, and usually worse in the morning. Swelling can be significant and cause a tight sensation to the skin
  • Redness may get worse over the first few days
  • Pinpoint bleeding is possible for the first few days
  • Itching
  • Your skin may feel dry or flaky. This dead skin is expected to start sloughing off after 3-4 days. Most patients complete this process by 5-7 days.
  • The skin will remain pink for some time after the treatment, for weeks to even months

PRE-TREATMENT INSTRUCTIONS

  • Discontinue skin irritants 1 week prior to your treatment (retinoids, salicylic acid, hydroquinone, glycolics, etc.)
  • Do not use medications that cause photosensitivity (doxycycline, minocycline for at least 3 days prior to your procedure).
  • Avoid sun exposure, tanning bed or sunless tanning products and use a broad spectrum sunscreen of SPF 30 or greater for the month prior to treatment.
  • Avoid deep facial peels for one month prior to treatment (this includes microdermabrasion, laser resurfacing or aggressive chemical peels)
  • Prepare vinegar soak solution and baggies of frozen peas
  • Arrive on the day of the procedure with clean skin, free of makeup
  • Let us know if you are prone to cold sores

POST-TREATMENT INSTRUCTIONS

  • If you’ve received oral pain medications or oral sedatives during treatment, You MUST have an adult drive you home from the facility. You will not be allowed to drive yourself or use public transportation.
  • Rest and sleep with your head elevated on at least three pillows for 3-4 days after the procedure
  • Apply ice packs (frozen peas) to help with the heat sensation and swelling, 20 minutes on/20 minutes off while you are awake for the first three days
  • Take prescribed medications as instructed
    • If you experience any general itching, wheezing, rash or tightness in the throat, stop taking all medications and contact AestheticEye Oculoplastic Surgeons immediately.
  • Avoid high heat, sun, blood thinners and alcohol
  • Minimal activity for the first 48 hours. Avoid house cleaning, furniture rearranging, etc. Relax and let your body heal. The less energy you exert, the more energy you will have to focus on healing.
  • Do not touch the skin or pick at the skin
  • Do not wear make-up
  • Avoid exercise: no perspiring, swimming or exposing skin to heat or sun
  • Avoid dusty environments, dirt or chemical contact (ie: hairspray)
  • Drink plenty of fluids.
  • Call our office if you have: SEVERE PAIN not responding to pain medication; SWELLING that is greater on one side than the other; incisions that are RED OR FEVERISH; a FEVER or if any other questions or concerns arise.
  • Keep any dressings ON, CLEAN and DRY. Do not remove them until instructed to do so.

POST-TREATMENT SKIN CARE INSTRUCTIONS DAY 0-4

  • Skin will be peeling and sloughing for the first 5-7 days
  • Only cleanse skin with vinegar soaks for the first 4 days. Apply vinegar soaks with clean paper gauze over the face for 15 minutes, 6-8 times a day for the first 2 days and then 4 times daily on days 3 and 4.
    • Vinegar solution recipe: one cup distilled water and 2 teaspoons of vinegar
    • Wash your hands
    • Dip gauze or paper towel into the solution and place over the lasered areas (it should be soaking wet and drippling)
    • Gently press onto the skin, but do not rub
    • You may store the solution in the refrigerator to keep it cold for your soaks
    • Apply thin layer of Aquaphor or CereVe healing ointment over the lasered area after each vinegar soak and any time the skin feels dry

POST-TREATMENT SKIN CARE INSTRUCTIONS DAY 5-7

  • The skin will be less red and should not feel uncomfortable.
  • Dryness, itchiness and skin peeling or flaking may occur.
  • Redness usually lasts 1-2 weeks and mild redness may be prolonged.
  • Gently wash your face twice daily with mild facial cleanser (CereVe bar soap or gentle cleanser) Do not rub the skin vigorously as the skin will be fragile.
  • Switch to using less occlusive moisturizer, like Epidermal Repair for two weeks. You may start using Alastin nectar at this point.
  • Apply a physical sunscreen (SPF 30 or greater) after the application of the moisturizer
  • Mineral makeup may be applied if desired once sunscreen is being used. We recommend Oxygenetix
  • Avoid direct exposure to the sun for the first 3 months (wear sunscreen and hat/sunglasses)

title: Sofwave Ultrasound Treatment Pre and Post Care Instructions
description: Achieve optimal lifting and tightening from your Sofwave treatment at AestheticEye. Use these preparation and aftercare tips to protect your results and ensure a smooth recovery.

headings.title: Sofwave Ultrasound Treatment-How to Maximize Your Results

html:
Sofwave Ultrasound Treatment-How to Maximize Your Results

Sofwave is a non-invasive next generation ultrasound treatment to lift, tighten, and tone the brow, face, neck and skin. It improves lines, wrinkles, and sagging skin without downtime.

PRE-TREATMENT INSTRUCTIONS

  1. Arrival and Preparation:
    • Arrive on time for your scheduled appointment. Avoid applying any skincare products, makeup, or sunscreen after your first cleansing of the day.
    • Ensure that you have eaten prior to your appointment to maintain comfort during the procedure.
    • Arrive jewelry-free and, if receiving a neck treatment, wear a V-neck top for easy access to the treatment area.
  2. Photos and Consent:
    • Photographs and consent documentation will be completed prior to treatment, if not already done.
  3. Pre-Treatment Cleansing and Numbing:
    • A team member will thoroughly cleanse the skin to remove any residual product or debris.
    • Topical numbing cream will be applied to the treatment area and will remain for approximately 30 minutes to enhance comfort during the procedure.
  4. Contraindications – Reasons to Avoid Sofwave:
    • Active cystic acne or open wounds in the treatment area
    • Metal implants within the treatment area
    • Recent dermal filler treatment in the treatment area (wait at least two weeks before and after Sofwave treatment)
    • Please notify our team if any of the above apply to you to determine if Sofwave is appropriate at this time.

POST-TREATMENT INSTRUCTIONS

  1. Expected Effects:
    • Mild redness and/or swelling may occur in the treated area and typically resolve within a few hours.
    • Warmth or tenderness in the treatment area may persist but should subside without intervention.
    • There should be no persistent pain after the procedure. Contact the office if discomfort persists.
  2. Skin Care:
    • You may resume your regular skincare routine immediately following the treatment.
    • Apply sunscreen with SPF 30 or higher to protect the treated area from UV exposure.
  3. Follow-Up:
    • Results develop gradually over time, with most patients noticing improvements as early as two weeks post-treatment. Full results typically appear within three months.
    • A follow-up appointment is recommended in 3-4 months for post-treatment photos and evaluation.
    • For optimal results, a series of one to two treatments is generally recommended, with maintenance sessions every 12 months.

If you have any questions or concerns regarding your Sofwave treatment, please do not hesitate to contact our office.

html:
Upper eyelid blepharoplasty, often known as an upper eyelid lift, is a transformative procedure for individuals looking to rejuvenate their appearance by addressing droopy upper eyelids. This common issue, often due to aging or genetics, can impact both your vision and overall look, making you appear tired or older. At AestheticEye in Cincinnati, OH, our board-certified oculoplastic surgeons, Dr. Ginger Henson and Dr. Jonathan Pargament, specialize in upper eyelid surgery to help you achieve a more youthful and refreshed appearance.

Blepahroplasty Quiz

What is Upper Blepharoplasty?

Upper blepharoplasty is a surgical procedure designed to correct issues with the upper eyelids. This surgery targets and removes excess skin, muscle, and sometimes fat from the upper eyelids, resulting in a smoother and more lifted appearance. Upper blepharoplasty effectively eliminates droopy upper eyelids, improving both your vision and aesthetic appeal.

Dr. Ginger Henson was a perfect choice for me! She did an excellent job. I had no pain and healed up better than ever! I’m so happy with the job she did for me!

Benefits of Upper Eyelid Surgery

View More Before & After Results

Choosing upper eyelid surgery at AestheticEye offers numerous benefits, including:

Enhanced Vision

Removing excess skin that droops over the eyelids can significantly improve your field of vision.

Rejuvenated Appearance

By eliminating sagging skin, upper eyelid surgery provides a more youthful and revitalized look.

Boosted Confidence

Achieving a more alert and refreshed appearance can enhance your self-esteem and confidence.

Book An Appointment (937) 907-9009

The Upper Eyelid Lift Procedure

At AestheticEye, our surgeons utilize advanced techniques to ensure the best possible outcomes for upper blepharoplasty. During the procedure, an incision is made along the natural crease of the upper eyelid. Through this incision, excess skin, muscle, and sometimes fat are removed or repositioned to create a smoother and more lifted contour. The incision is then carefully closed, resulting in minimal scarring that is typically well-hidden within the natural folds of the eyelid.

Healing and Outcomes

Recovery from upper eyelid surgery is generally smooth, with most patients experiencing mild swelling and bruising for the first week or two. Cold compresses and prescribed medications can help manage these symptoms. Most patients return to their normal activities within 10-14 days. Achieving and maintaining beautiful, healthy skin requires more than over-the-counter products found at your local drugstore. The Science Behind Medical-Grade Skincare

What distinguishes medical-grade skincare from department store alternatives? The difference lies in the formulation, concentration, and delivery of active ingredients. Medical-grade products, also known as cosmeceuticals, bridge the gap between cosmetics and pharmaceuticals. They undergo extensive clinical trials, contain pharmaceutical-grade ingredients at therapeutic concentrations, and are designed to penetrate deeper layers of the skin where real transformation occurs.

These professional products are exclusively available through medical practices and licensed professionals who understand skin physiology and can recommend appropriate regimens based on your unique needs. The formulations we offer at AestheticEye work synergistically with our surgical and non-surgical treatments, helping to prepare skin for procedures, accelerate healing, and maintain your beautiful results long-term.

Why Choose Professional Skincare Products?

Investing in medical-grade skincare offers several significant advantages over retail alternatives:

  • Higher Concentrations of Active Ingredients: Pharmaceutical-grade formulations contain potent levels of proven ingredients like retinoids, peptides, growth factors, and antioxidants that deliver visible results
  • Superior Penetration: Advanced delivery systems ensure active ingredients reach deeper skin layers where cellular transformation occurs
  • Clinically Proven Results: Extensive research and clinical trials validate the efficacy of medical-grade products
  • Complementary to Treatments: Professional skincare enhances and prolongs the results of surgical procedures, injectables, and laser treatments
  • Customized Recommendations: Our expert team evaluates your skin type, concerns, and goals to create a personalized regimen
  • Quality and Purity: Pharmaceutical-grade ingredients meet stringent quality standards for safety and effectiveness
  • Professional Guidance: Access to ongoing support and adjustments to your skincare routine as your needs evolve

“Beautiful results from any aesthetic procedure begin with healthy skin,” notes Dr. Henson. “The right medical-grade skincare regimen is essential for preparing skin for treatment, supporting optimal healing, and maintaining your rejuvenated appearance for years to come.”

The Alastin product line includes specialized formulations designed to prepare skin before procedures, accelerate healing afterward, and maintain results long-term. These products are particularly effective when used in conjunction with surgical procedures, injectables, and laser treatments, making them an essential component of comprehensive aesthetic care.

Plated Skin Science

Plated Skin Science represents a groundbreaking advancement in regenerative skincare, harnessing the power of platelet-derived exosomes to rejuvenate aging skin at the cellular level. Their proprietary Renewosome™ technology delivers a pure, potent blend of growth factors and signaling molecules that communicate directly with skin cells, triggering natural renewal processes that restore youthful vitality.

Unlike traditional anti-aging products that primarily work on the skin’s surface, Plated penetrates deeply to stimulate collagen production, improve texture and tone, and enhance overall skin health from within. Clinically proven to reduce fine lines, improve radiance, and restore a more youthful appearance, Plated offers professional-grade results without needles or downtime. This cutting-edge line translates decades of regenerative medicine research into elegant daily skincare that delivers transformative results for patients seeking the most advanced scientific solutions available.

SkinCeuticals

SkinCeuticals has earned its reputation as a gold standard in medical-grade skincare through decades of pioneering research and unwavering commitment to scientific excellence. Founded by a renowned dermatologist, this pharmaceutical-grade line is built on three foundational principles: prevent future damage, protect healthy skin, and correct previous damage. Every SkinCeuticals formulation undergoes rigorous clinical testing to ensure optimal efficacy, stability, and absorption.

The brand is perhaps best known for its exceptional antioxidant serums, particularly the iconic C E Ferulic, which provides advanced environmental protection while improving signs of aging and photodamage. Their evidence-based approach ensures that each product delivers measurable results, making SkinCeuticals a trusted choice among dermatologists and plastic surgeons worldwide. Whether you’re seeking prevention, correction, or maintenance, SkinCeuticals provides scientifically-validated formulations that deliver on their promises.

Image Skincare

Image Skincare combines cutting-edge scientific innovation with the power of nature to create effective, results-driven formulations for every skin type and concern. This physician-founded line features high-performance botanical ingredients alongside proven pharmaceutical compounds, offering a balanced approach to skin health that addresses both immediate concerns and long-term wellness.

Ptosis, commonly known as droopy eyelids, can affect both appearance and vision, making daily activities challenging. At AestheticEye in Cincinnati, OH, our board-certified oculoplastic surgeons, Dr. Ginger Henson and Dr. Jonathan Pargament, specialize in diagnosing and treating ptosis with precision and care. Serving Cincinnati, Dayton, our team is dedicated to helping you achieve a more youthful look and improved eye function through advanced ptosis repair surgery.

Understanding Ptosis and Its Impact

Ptosis is characterized by the drooping of one or both upper eyelids. This condition can be congenital (present at birth) or acquired later in life due to aging, injury, or neurological disorders. Ptosis can range from mild to severe, with significant cases obstructing vision and affecting daily life.

Symptoms of Ptosis

Drooping of the Upper Eyelid

One or both eyelids may droop, sometimes covering the pupil.

Impaired Vision

Severe ptosis can block normal vision, making activities like reading or driving difficult.

Eye Fatigue

Straining to lift the eyelids can lead to eye fatigue and discomfort.

Asymmetrical Appearance

Ptosis can cause an uneven look, affecting overall facial symmetry.

Advanced Droopy Eyelid Correction at AestheticEye

At AestheticEye, we offer advanced solutions for droopy eyelid correction, tailored to meet each patient’s unique needs. Our comprehensive approach ensures that both aesthetic and functional concerns are addressed.

Upper Eyelid Ptosis Surgery

Upper eyelid ptosis surgery, or ptosis repair surgery, involves tightening the muscles that lift the eyelid. This procedure can be performed using various techniques, depending on the severity of the ptosis and the underlying cause.

Levator Muscle Resection

Involves shortening the levator muscle to lift the eyelid.

Müller Muscle Resection

A less invasive procedure that targets the smaller Müller muscle for minor ptosis.

Frontalis Sling

Uses a sling to connect the eyelid to the forehead muscle, allowing the brow to lift the eyelid in cases of severe ptosis or weak levator muscles.

How SkinPen® Works: Precision Meets Regeneration

SkinPen works by creating thousands of controlled micro-injuries to the skin’s surface, triggering the body’s natural wound-healing process. This stimulates collagen and elastin production—the building blocks of healthy, youthful skin. According to the American Society of Plastic Surgeons, microneedling has seen a popularity surge of 55% in recent years, driven by its ability to improve skin tone and reduce signs of aging without invasive measures.

The three-phase process includes:

Inflammation

Tiny punctures trigger an immune response, cleansing the wound and increasing blood flow.

Proliferation

New tissue and blood vessels begin to form.

Remodeling

Collagen and elastin strengthen the skin for lasting firmness and elasticity.

What Can SkinPen® Treat?

This versatile treatment is effective for a wide range of skin concerns, including:

  • Fine lines and wrinkles
  • Acne scars
  • Enlarged pores

SkinPen can be safely used on the face, neck, décolletage, and other body areas to achieve a more youthful and even-toned appearance.

How Dermaplaning Works

Dermaplaning involves using a sterile, medical-grade blade to gently exfoliate the outermost layer of skin. This layer often harbors buildup from environmental exposure, residual skincare products, and natural oils. By sweeping the blade across the skin’s surface, the treatment removes:

  • Dead skin cells
  • Fine facial hair (peach fuzz)
  • Dull or dry patches
  • Minor surface irregularities

The result is a polished, ultra-smooth canvas that reflects light more evenly, creating a soft and healthy glow.

Who is a Good Candidate for Dermaplaning?

Dermaplaning is well-suited for most healthy adults, particularly those who:

  • Want to brighten dull skin
  • Experience dry or flaky skin
  • Are prone to breakouts from clogged pores

No. Dermaplaning does not change the texture or color of your hair.

title: Post-Operative Instructions
description: Follow these essential post-operative care instructions to support healing and minimize complications after your procedure.
html:
The following instructions should be followed closely except when overruled by specific procedural instructions. You must follow your surgeon’s instructions as indicated for your specific surgery. Please notify AestheticEye Oculoplastic Surgeons of any unusual changes in your condition and feel free to call the office with any questions. 

  1. You MUST have an adult drive you home from the facility. You will not be allowed to drive yourself or use public transportation.
  2. After surgery, you must have a responsible adult stay with you for a minimum of 24 hours.
  3. The effects of anesthesia can persist for up to 24 hours. You must exercise caution before engaging in any activity that could be harmful to yourself or others.
  4. Drink plenty of fluids to help rid your body of the drugs used in surgery.
  5. Avoid the use of alcoholic beverages for the first 24 hours and while pain medications are being used.
  6. Take only medications that have been prescribed by AestheticEye Oculoplastic Surgeons for your postoperative care and take them according to the instructions on the bottle. Pain medications may make you feel “spacey,” therefore, it’s best for someone else to give you these medications and ensure the appropriate timeline is being followed.
  7. If you experience any general itching, wheezing, rash or tightness in the throat, stop taking all medications and contact AestheticEye Oculoplastic Surgeons immediately.
  8. Keep any dressings ON, CLEAN and DRY. Do not remove them until you are instructed to do so.
  9. Minimal activity for the first 48 hours.
  10. Cold Compress: Apply cold compresses (e.g., ice packs or chilled gauze) for 2 to 3 days after surgery to reduce swelling and bruising—discontinue at bedtime.
  11. Head Elevation: Sleep with your head elevated on 2-3 pillows to minimize swelling for 5 days.
  12. Minimal Activity: Avoid bending over, lifting heavy objects, or straining for 1-2 WEEKS post operation.
  13. Showering: You may shower 1-2 days after surgery but avoid direct water pressure on your face.
  14. No Rubbing or Touching: Avoid rubbing, touching, or applying pressure to your eyes.
  15. No Makeup or Contacts: Avoid makeup, false eyelashes, and contact lenses for at least 14 days.
  16. Limit sun exposure—wear sunglasses and sunscreen if going outside.
  17. No smoking for two weeks or alcohol for 24 hours and pain medication is being used, as they delay healing.
  18. You can expect:
    1. Swelling & Bruising: Peaks within 48 hours, gradually subsides over 1–2 weeks.
    2. Mild Discomfort or Dry Eyes are common. Use artificial tears if needed.
    3. Tightness or Numbness are common and temporary.
    4. Slight oozing from wound edges.
    5. Possible bloodshot eyes.
  19. Call our office if you experience any of the following:
    1. Excessive swelling or worsening pain after 48 hours that isn’t remedied with pain medication.
    2. Sudden vision changes, severe eye pain, or excessive bleeding from the incision.
    3. Signs of infection: Redness, warmth, pus, or fever over 100.4°F.
  20. As time goes by and you are healing, the following guidelines apply:
    1. Patients return to work 7 to 10 days following surgery depending on the type of work done.
    2. All normal activities may be resumed approximately 2 weeks post op

html:
Facial fat transfers, also known as fat grafting or fat injections, are advanced procedures used to restore volume, enhance facial contours, and improve overall facial aesthetics. At AestheticEye in Cincinnati, OH, our board-certified oculoplastic surgeons, Dr. Ginger Henson and Dr. Jonathan Pargament, specialize in facial fat transfers, particularly in relation to reconstructive and cosmetic eye surgeries. Serving patients in Cincinnati, Dayton, our team is dedicated to providing personalized care and exceptional results.

The Benefits of Fat Transfer Surgery at AestheticEye

Facial fat transfers offer a natural solution to volume loss, allowing for the restoration of youthful contours and the correction of asymmetries. The procedure uses your body’s own fat, which is harvested from areas like the abdomen or thighs, purified, and then injected into the target areas of the face.
