How Facial Fat Transfers Enhance Reconstructive Eye Surgeries

Facial fat transfers are particularly beneficial when used in conjunction with reconstructive eye surgeries. They can help address volume loss around the eyes, improve the results of eyelid surgeries, and enhance overall facial harmony.

Restoring Volume

Fat grafting can replenish lost volume in the periocular area, providing a more balanced and youthful appearance.

Enhancing Eyelid Reconstruction

Fat transfers can complement eyelid reconstruction by filling in hollow areas and smoothing transitions between different facial regions.

Improving Facial Symmetry

Fat injections can correct asymmetries that may result from trauma or previous surgeries.

Book An Appointment (937) 907-9009

The Facial Fat Transfer Procedure

At AestheticEye, our surgeons utilize advanced techniques to ensure the best possible outcomes for facial fat transfers. The procedure involves several key steps:

Consultation and Evaluation

During your initial consultation, Dr. Henson or Dr. Pargament will perform a thorough evaluation to understand your goals and assess the areas that would benefit from fat grafting. They will develop a personalized treatment plan tailored to your needs.

Harvesting the Fat

The first step in the procedure is to harvest fat from a donor site, typically the abdomen or thighs. This is done using gentle liposuction techniques to minimize trauma to the fat cells.

Purifying the Fat

The harvested fat is then purified to remove any impurities and ensure that only healthy fat cells are used for the grafting process.

Injecting the Fat

The purified fat is carefully injected into the target areas of the face using fine cannulas. Our surgeons use precise techniques to ensure even distribution and natural-looking results.

Recovery and Results

Recovery from facial fat transfer is generally smooth, with most patients experiencing mild swelling and bruising for the first week or two. The results of fat grafting are long-lasting, providing a natural enhancement to your facial contours and overall appearance.

Book An Appointment (937) 907-9009

Frequently Asked Questions | Facial Fat Transfers

How Long Do the Results of Facial Fat Transfers Last?

The results of facial fat transfers can be long-lasting, often several years. Unlike synthetic fillers, which are eventually absorbed by the body, the transferred fat cells can integrate with the surrounding tissues and provide lasting volume.

Can Facial Fat Transfers Be Combined with Other Procedures?

Yes, facial fat transfers can be combined with other procedures, such as eyelid reconstruction or facelifts, to achieve more comprehensive results. Combining treatments can enhance overall facial harmony and improve the aesthetic outcome.

What Are the Advantages of Using My Own Fat for Injections?

Using your own fat for injections has several advantages, including a lower risk of allergic reactions and a more natural look and feel compared to synthetic fillers. Additionally, fat grafting can provide a dual benefit by contouring the donor site through liposuction.

Is the Fat Transfer Procedure Painful?

The procedure is performed under local anesthesia, so you will not feel pain during the injections. Post-operative discomfort is usually minimal and can be managed with over-the-counter pain medications.

How Soon Will I See the Results of Fat Grafting?

Initial results can be seen immediately after the procedure, although some swelling and bruising may be present. The final results become more apparent as the swelling subsides, typically within a few weeks.

Are There Any Risks Associated with Facial Fat Transfers?

As with any surgical procedure, there are potential risks, including infection, uneven results, and fat resorption. These risks are minimized when the procedure is performed by experienced oculoplastic surgeons like Dr. Henson and Dr. Pargament at AestheticEye.

Sun exposure, smoking, and pollution can accelerate the aging process by damaging the skin.

Lower blepharoplasty is a surgical procedure designed to correct issues with the lower eyelids. Is Under Eye Bag Removal Covered by Insurance?

Under eye bag removal is typically considered a cosmetic procedure and is not covered by insurance. However, if the surgery is performed to improve vision or address a medical condition, insurance may cover some or all of the costs.

Recovery involves mild swelling and bruising for the first week or two. Patients can use cold compresses and prescribed medications to manage discomfort. Most return to normal activities within 10-14 days.

Under Eye Bag Causes

Several factors can contribute to the development of lower eyelid bags, including:

Aging

As we age, the skin and muscles around the eyes become weaker, and fat that is normally confined to the area around the eyes can move into the lower eyelids, causing the appearance of bags.

Genetics

For some individuals, lower eyelid bags are a hereditary trait. If your parents or grandparents had under-eye bags, you are more likely to develop them as well.

Lifestyle Factors

Lack of sleep, stress, and poor diet can all contribute to the development of lower eyelid bags. Allergies and fluid retention due to high salt intake can also cause puffiness under the eyes.

Sun Exposure

Excessive sun exposure can weaken the skin and contribute to the breakdown of collagen and elastin, leading to sagging and the formation of under-eye bags.

While it’s not always possible to prevent lower eyelid bags entirely, maintaining a healthy lifestyle, getting enough sleep, managing stress, and protecting your skin from sun damage can help reduce their severity.

Non-surgical treatments like chemical peels, and laser therapy can be effective for mild to moderate cases of lower eyelid bags. These treatments can provide noticeable improvements with minimal downtime.

headings.title: The Role of an Oculoplastic Surgeon

html:
Dec 10, 2024

Excessive tearing, medically known as epiphora, can be a frustrating and uncomfortable condition. It can interfere with daily activities, cause irritation, and even affect your vision. Fortunately, there are effective surgical solutions available at AestheticEye in Dayton, OH, to address this issue. Here’s what you need to know about repairing excessive tearing and how our expert oculoplastic surgeons can help.

Understanding Excessive Tearing

Excessive tearing can occur due to various reasons, including blocked tear ducts, eyelid malposition, or overproduction of tears. When the tear drainage system isn’t functioning properly, tears can overflow onto your face instead of draining through the nasal passages. This can lead to constant tearing, eye irritation, and even infections.

The Role of an Oculoplastic Surgeon

Oculoplastic surgeons, such as Dr. Ginger Henson and Dr. Jonathan Pargament, specialize in the anatomy and function of the eyelids and tear drainage system. Their expertise allows them to accurately diagnose the underlying cause of excessive tearing and recommend the most appropriate surgical solution.

Surgical Solutions for Excessive Tearing

There are several surgical options to address excessive tearing, depending on the root cause of the problem:

  1. Dacryocystorhinostomy (DCR): This is a common procedure used to treat blocked tear ducts. During DCR, the surgeon creates a new drainage pathway from the tear sac into the nasal cavity, bypassing the blockage. This allows tears to drain normally, reducing or eliminating excessive tearing.
  1. Punctoplasty: If the tear ducts are partially blocked, punctoplasty may be recommended. This procedure involves widening the opening of the tear ducts to improve tear drainage. It’s a less invasive option that can effectively reduce tearing.
  1. Eyelid Surgery: In cases where eyelid malposition (such as ectropion or entropion) contributes to excessive tearing, corrective eyelid surgery may be necessary. Adjusting the position of the eyelids can help restore proper tear drainage and reduce tearing.

Benefits of Surgical Treatment

Choosing surgical treatment for excessive tearing can provide significant benefits:

  • Improved Comfort: Surgical solutions can alleviate the constant irritation and discomfort associated with excessive tearing. You’ll no longer need to frequently wipe away tears or deal with the associated skin irritation.
  • Enhanced Vision: By addressing the underlying cause of excessive tearing, surgery can improve your vision and reduce the risk of infections or other complications.
  • Long-Term Relief: Surgical treatments offer long-lasting results, providing you with a permanent solution to excessive tearing.

Personalized Care at AestheticEye

At AestheticEye, we understand that each patient’s needs are unique. Our experienced oculoplastic surgeons will conduct a thorough evaluation to determine the cause of your excessive tearing and develop a personalized treatment plan. We prioritize your comfort and safety, ensuring you receive the highest standard of care.

If you’re tired of constantly tearing up and are seeking a lasting solution, we invite you to schedule a consultation with Dr. Henson or Dr. Pargament at AestheticEye in Dayton, OH. Let us help you regain comfort and clarity with our specialized surgical treatments for excessive tearing.

description: If you've ever experienced a sudden twitching of your eyelid, you're not alone. Eye twitching, medically known as blepharospasm, is a common condition

headings.title: When to Seek Help for Eye Twitching

html:
Mar 18, 2025

If you’ve ever experienced a sudden twitching of your eyelid, you’re not alone. Eye twitching, medically known as blepharospasm, is a common condition that can affect anyone, regardless of age or gender. While it’s often harmless, it can be quite bothersome and may indicate underlying stress or fatigue. AestheticEye in Cincinnati, OH, explores the causes of eye twitching, how to manage it and when to seek professional help.

What is Blepharospasm?

The National Eye Institute defines Blepharospasm (also called benign essential blepharospasm) as “blinking or other eyelid movements, like twitching, that you can’t control.” They also report that sometimes blepharospasm runs in families, and women ages 40 to 60 are more likely to develop it.

This condition is an involuntary contraction of the muscles around the eye that can lead to repetitive blinking or spasms. It can occur in one or both eyes and may be triggered by various factors. While it is generally not serious, chronic twitching can be annoying and may affect daily life.

The National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke characterizes blepharospasm as a progressive condition that can worsen over time without treatment.

Common Causes of Eye Twitching

  • Stress and Fatigue: One of the most common triggers of eye twitching is stress. High levels of stress can cause muscles to twitch, including those around the eyes. Similarly, fatigue and lack of sleep can exacerbate this condition.
  • Caffeine and Alcohol: Consuming excessive caffeine or alcohol can lead to increased muscle activity, including spasms in the eye. Reducing your intake may help alleviate symptoms.
  • Dry Eyes: Many people experience eye twitching due to dry eyes, especially those who spend long hours in front of screens. Dryness can irritate the eyelids and result in twitching.
  • Eye Strain: Prolonged screen time or poor vision can lead to eye strain, which in turn can cause muscle spasms. Regular breaks and proper eye care can help reduce strain.
  • Nutritional Deficiencies: A lack of essential nutrients, such as magnesium, can also contribute to muscle spasms, including those in the eyelids.

When to Seek Help for Eye Twitching

In most cases, eye twitching is benign and resolves on its own. However, if twitching persists for several weeks, is accompanied by other symptoms (such as pain, swelling or changes in vision) or interferes significantly with daily activities, it’s essential to consult a healthcare professional. Persistent blepharospasm may indicate an underlying condition that requires attention. Our AestheticEye team has medical treatments, surgical and non-surgical options for treating persistent eye twitching.

Cincinnati OH Eye Twitching Treatment

Eye twitching can be an annoying yet common issue affecting many. Understanding the potential causes and implementing some simple lifestyle changes may help mitigate this condition. If you are struggling with eye twitching or blepharospasm, contact AestheticEye today to schedule a consultation. Our expert surgeons, Dr. Henson and Dr. Pargament, are here to help you explore your treatment options and develop a personalized plan to improve your comfort and quality of life.

At AestheticEye in Cincinnati, OH, we understand how much your eyes and forehead impact the way you look and how others perceive you. Over time, the natural aging process can cause the upper eyelids to droop and the brows to sag, leading to a tired, angry, or worn-out appearance—even if you feel energetic and youthful on the inside. Combining brow lift and eyelid lift (blepharoplasty) procedures offers a powerful, balanced approach to facial rejuvenation, giving you smoother, more open eyes and a refreshed expression.

Refresh Your Eyes and Facial Expression with Balanced Rejuvenation

Individually, both brow and eyelid lift procedures can deliver impressive results. A brow lift elevates sagging brows, smooths deep forehead lines, and reduces heaviness around the upper face. An eyelid lift focuses on removing excess skin, puffiness, or fat from the upper and/or lower eyelids, making the eyes appear brighter and more youthful.

However, these areas are closely connected. If one is treated without the other, the results can sometimes look incomplete or out of balance. For example, lifting the eyelids without addressing low brows might leave the forehead looking heavy. Similarly, elevating the brows without improving eyelid droopiness may not fully open the eyes.

By combining both procedures, you can achieve harmony between the eyes, brows, and forehead. This approach creates a natural-looking, refreshed appearance without overdoing it. Patients often find that their entire facial expression looks lighter, friendlier, and more awake after a combined brow and eyelid lift.

Streamlined Surgery and Recovery

Another advantage of combining these procedures is convenience. When done together, brow and eyelid lifts require only one surgical appointment, one round of anesthesia, and one recovery period. This can reduce overall downtime and is often more cost-effective compared to staging the procedures separately.

Most patients can expect initial swelling and bruising to subside within two to three weeks, with final results becoming clearer as the healing process continues over the following months. Our team will guide you through every step, from consultation to recovery, to ensure a smooth experience.

The Importance of Choosing an Experienced Oculoplastic Surgeon

When it comes to surgery around the eyes, expertise matters. The eyes are delicate, complex structures, and achieving natural, balanced results requires advanced skill and a deep understanding of facial anatomy. That’s why it’s essential to choose a board-certified oculoplastic surgeon with specialized training in cosmetic and reconstructive procedures of the eyelids and brow.

At AestheticEye, our team is led by highly trained oculoplastic specialists who focus exclusively on the eyes and surrounding areas. We take a tailored, precision-based approach to every procedure, ensuring that your results enhance—not change—your natural appearance.

If you’re ready to restore a youthful, refreshed look and bring balance back to your facial features, schedule a consultation with us today. We’ll help you explore whether a combined brow and eyelid lift is right for you. Call our clinic in Cincinnati, OH, to book your appointment.

title: Reconstructive Options After Mohs Surgery for Eyelid Skin Cancer
description: The eyelids are one of the most delicate and complex areas of the face—and unfortunately, they are also vulnerable to skin cancer. Due to their thin skin

images.alt: Close-up of a person's eye with smooth, natural makeup and well-groomed eyebrow. The skin appears clear and well-lit.

headings.title: The Importance of an Experienced Oculoplastic Surgeon

html:
May 13, 2025

The eyelids are one of the most delicate and complex areas of the face—and unfortunately, they are also vulnerable to skin cancer. Due to their thin skin and frequent sun exposure, the eyelids are a common site for basal cell carcinoma and squamous cell carcinoma, the two most prevalent forms of skin cancer.

When skin cancer develops on or around the eyelid, Mohs surgery is often recommended. Mohs is a highly effective surgical technique that removes cancerous tissue layer by layer while preserving as much healthy tissue as possible. However, because of the eyelid’s functional and cosmetic importance, removing the cancer often leaves defects that require precise, specialized reconstruction.

At AestheticEye in Springboro, OH, serving the greater Dayton and Cincinnati area, we offer advanced reconstructive solutions to restore both the appearance and function of the eyelid following Mohs surgery.

The Importance of an Experienced Oculoplastic Surgeon

Eyelid reconstruction is not like standard skin repair. The eyelids protect the eyes, maintain tear drainage, and contribute to facial expression. Poor reconstruction can lead to functional problems such as dry eye, exposure keratitis, or vision impairment, as well as noticeable cosmetic deformities.

That’s why it’s essential to choose a board-certified oculoplastic surgeon—a specialist with advanced training in both ophthalmology and plastic surgery—to perform your reconstructive procedure. At AestheticEye, our team has the skill and experience to restore both the form and function of your eyelids after skin cancer surgery.

Advanced Techniques in Eyelid Reconstruction

Every case of eyelid reconstruction is unique, depending on the size and location of the defect left after Mohs surgery. We offer a range of advanced surgical techniques tailored to each patient’s specific needs:

  • Local Flaps: In many cases, we can use nearby eyelid or facial tissue to repair the defect. This method, called a local flap, ensures a natural match in skin color and texture while minimizing scarring.
  • Skin Grafts: When local tissue is not sufficient, we may use skin grafts from another part of the body—such as behind the ear or from the upper eyelid—to reconstruct the area.
  • Eyelid Margin Reconstruction: If the cancer removal involves the eyelid margin, specialized techniques are used to restore the delicate edge of the eyelid. Proper reconstruction of the margin is crucial to ensure eye protection and normal tear drainage
  • Composite Reconstruction: For larger or more complex defects, composite reconstruction may be necessary. This technique involves combining skin, muscle, and sometimes cartilage to rebuild the eyelid and restore its protective function.

Restore Function and Appearance

At AestheticEye, we understand the physical and emotional impact of skin cancer and facial reconstruction. Our goal is to help you heal, restore eyelid function, and regain confidence in your appearance.

If you or a loved one requires eyelid reconstruction after Mohs surgery, contact AestheticEye in Springboro today to schedule a consultation. Our experienced team proudly serves patients throughout Dayton and Cincinnati.

The eyes are often the first place we show signs of aging, and the first feature people notice. If you’re dealing with drooping eyelids, puffy under-eye bags, or an overall tired appearance, eyelid surgery (blepharoplasty) could offer the natural-looking refresh you’ve been searching for.

At AestheticEye, our fellowship-trained, board-certified oculoplastic surgeons — Dr. Ginger Henson and Dr. Jonathan Pargament — specialize in cosmetic and functional eyelid surgery in Cincinnati, Springboro, and the greater Dayton, Ohio area. Blepharoplasty is not only popular — it’s one of the most effective and highest-rated facial procedures. According to the American Society of Plastic Surgeons, more than 115,000 blepharoplasty procedures were performed in 2023, making it one of the top five cosmetic surgeries in the country.

Here are six signs it may be time to consider eyelid surgery:

1. Sagging Eyelids Are Impacting Your Vision

When upper eyelids begin to hang over the lash line, it’s more than just a cosmetic concern — it could be functional ptosis, a condition that can limit your field of vision. If you find yourself tilting your head back or raising your eyebrows to see clearly, eyelid surgery may be medically necessary, and insurance might cover part of the procedure. Studies show that patients with ptosis can regain up to 50% of their visual field after surgery.

2. You Look Tired — Even When You’re Not

Persistent puffiness, dark circles, or sagging skin around the eyes can create a fatigued or worn-out appearance. A lower or upper blepharoplasty can smooth and refresh the eye area, helping you look more alert and energized while still looking like yourself.

3. Eye Makeup Disappears or Smudges Easily

If drooping upper eyelid skin hides or distorts your makeup, eyelid surgery can restore space on the upper lid and enhance your natural contours. This not only improves the application of cosmetics but also helps define your eyes and restore youthful balance.

4. People Keep Asking If You’re Upset or Tired

Friends or coworkers asking if you’re okay — even when you feel great — is a common complaint we hear from new patients. Eyelid sagging can alter your resting facial expression, making you appear sad, tired, or even angry. Eyelid surgery can help realign your outer appearance with how you actually feel.

5. Daily Activities Like Reading or Driving Are Becoming Challenging

Significant eyelid drooping can interfere with day-to-day tasks like reading, working on a computer, or driving. Many patients subconsciously lift their brows to compensate, which often leads to forehead tension and neck strain. Blepharoplasty offers both cosmetic and functional relief in these cases.

6. You Want a Long-Lasting, Natural Result — Not a “Surgical” Look

At AestheticEye, we believe in enhancing your features without changing your identity. Dr. Henson and Dr. Pargament use advanced oculoplastic techniques to deliver precise, natural-looking results. As fellowship-trained oculofacial surgeons, they understand the delicate structures of the eyelids and face — ensuring safety, symmetry, and subtlety.

In fact, over 92% of patients who undergo blepharoplasty report high satisfaction and say they would choose the procedure again (RealSelf.com).

Most patients return to their usual activities within 7 to 10 days, with full results becoming visible as swelling subsides over a few weeks. For many, the improvements last for five to ten years or longer.

html:
Aug 11, 2025

Facial reanimation surgery is a specialized field of oculofacial plastic surgery that aims to restore movement and symmetry in the face, particularly for individuals experiencing facial paralysis or weakness due to various conditions, such as Bell’s palsy, stroke, trauma or congenital issues. At AestheticEye in Cincinnati, OH, we prioritize the physical and emotional well-being of our patients, offering highly skilled surgical interventions tailored to individual needs.

Understanding Facial Reanimation Surgery

Facial animation is vital for non-verbal communication and self-expression. When this ability is compromised, it can significantly affect a person’s quality of life. The American Academy of Ophthalmology reports that, “Socially, the loss of facial expressiveness leads to negative interpersonal interactions and self-image. Loss of facial expression negatively impacts emotional well-being, leading to feelings of isolation, embarrassment, and an overall decrease in quality of life.”

Facial reanimation surgery encompasses several techniques designed to restore facial movement and symmetry, enhancing both appearance and function.

Eyelid Weight Implants

For patients experiencing incomplete eyelid closure due to facial paralysis, eyelid weight implants provide a practical solution. These small weights are inserted into the upper eyelid, allowing gravity to assist in closing the eye during blinking and sleeping. This procedure not only prevents complications such as dryness and irritation but also improves the aesthetic appearance of the eyes.

Nerve and Muscle Transfers

Another innovative approach in facial reanimation involves transferring nerves and muscles from other parts of the body to the face. This technique can help restore functionality and movement. For example, the functional nerve from a nearby muscle is connected to the facial nerve, allowing the muscle to regain some level of control. This surgery can be particularly effective for patients with nerve damage resulting from trauma or surgery.

Brow Lift and Eyelid Lift Procedures

Often, facial reanimation necessitates not only the correction of movement but also the overall facial appearance. Brow lifts and eyelid lifts are commonly performed to improve facial symmetry and enhance visual function. These procedures can address sagging brows and eyelids, contributing to a more youthful and alert appearance while also facilitating better vision.

When Is Facial Reanimation Surgery Needed?

The need for facial reanimation surgery arises from various circumstances, primarily when individuals experience:

  • Facial Paralysis: Conditions such as Bell’s palsy or those resulting from traumatic injury can lead to nerve damage and facial weakness.
  • Congenital Disorders: Some individuals are born with conditions that affect their facial functionality, necessitating surgical intervention for improvement.
  • Post-Surgical Complications: In some cases, previous surgeries might inadvertently affect facial nerves and muscles, leading to loss of movement.

Commitment to Excellence at AestheticEye

At AestheticEye, we are dedicated to providing the highest standard of care in oculofacial plastic surgery. Our experienced surgeons, Dr. Ginger Henson and Dr. Jonathan Pargament, possess extensive training in this field, allowing them to implement the latest surgical techniques with precision and artistry. We understand that each patient has unique needs, and we take pride in offering personalized treatment plans tailored to restore both function and beauty.

Situated in Cincinnati and Dayton, AestheticEye combines state-of-the-art facilities with a compassionate approach. We believe that your eyes and face are integral to your identity and self-esteem, and our goal is to enhance your natural beauty while improving your vision and comfort.

Frequently Asked Questions about Facial Reanimation Surgery

What can I expect during the recovery process?

Recovery times vary depending on the specific type of surgery performed, but generally, patients can expect swelling and bruising that may take several weeks to subside. Our team will provide you with detailed post-operative care instructions to ensure a smooth recovery.

Are there any risks associated with facial reanimation surgery?

Like any surgical procedure, facial reanimation surgery carries risks, including infection, scarring and dissatisfaction with the aesthetic results. Our surgeons thoroughly discuss these risks during consultations to ensure that patients make informed decisions.

How long do the results of the surgery last?

The longevity of results depends on the specific procedure performed. Many patients enjoy lasting improvements in facial movement and appearance; however, periodic evaluations may be necessary to determine if follow-up procedures are required.

Will my insurance cover facial reanimation surgery?

Insurance coverage for facial reanimation surgery can vary based on the medical necessity of the procedure. Our team can assist you in navigating insurance options and guide on obtaining pre-approval if needed.

How do I decide if facial reanimation surgery is right for me?

The decision to undergo facial reanimation surgery should be made in consultation with a qualified oculofacial plastic surgeon. At AestheticEye, we will assess your specific condition, discuss your goals and determine the most appropriate surgical options to achieve desired outcomes.

Schedule Your Consultation

If you’re seeking to restore facial harmony and regain functionality through facial reanimation surgery, we invite you to contact AestheticEye. Our expert team is here to provide comprehensive care in a supportive environment. With our dedication to excellence and personalized patient care, you can trust that you’re in the best hands at AestheticEye in Cincinnati, OH.

At AestheticEye in Springboro, we help patients in Cincinnati, Dayton, and surrounding Ohio communities rejuvenate their facial expressions with advanced brow lift surgery.

What Happens When the Brows Begin to Fall?

Aging leads to the gradual loss of collagen and elasticity in the skin. Over time, this causes the eyebrows to droop, especially at the outer edges. This sagging effect can weigh down the upper eyelids and deepen forehead wrinkles, giving the appearance of a permanent scowl or frown.

This phenomenon, known as brow ptosis, doesn’t just change how others see you—it can affect how you see yourself. Many patients say they feel youthful and energetic on the inside, but their appearance tells a different story.

How a Brow Lift Helps

A brow lift, also called a forehead lift, surgically elevates the position of the eyebrows. It smooths out deep lines across the forehead, reduces frown lines between the brows, and opens the upper eye area. The result? A brighter, more alert, and naturally refreshed expression—without looking “overdone.”

For patients in the Dayton and Cincinnati area, a brow lift at AestheticEye offers a precise, personalized approach. Because we specialize in oculoplastic surgery, we consider both functional and aesthetic factors in every case, ensuring balance and long-lasting results.

Some benefits of a brow lift include:

  • Restores a natural, youthful arch to the brows
  • Reduces the appearance of heaviness over the eyes
  • Diminishes deep forehead creases and vertical “11” lines
  • Lifts the upper face for a more rested, pleasant expression
  • Often combined with eyelid surgery for total eye rejuvenation

In many cases, a brow lift can even improve peripheral vision if sagging brows have begun to obstruct the upper visual field.

Brow Lift Statistics and Trends

According to the American Society of Plastic Surgeons, more than 13,000 brow lift procedures are performed each year in the U.S. While traditionally more popular among women, brow lifts are increasingly sought by men who want to restore a more confident, approachable appearance.

The procedure is commonly done in patients aged 40 to 65, but individuals outside this range can still be great candidates depending on facial anatomy and goals.

Why Choose AestheticEye in Springboro?

At AestheticEye, our board-certified oculoplastic surgeons have advanced training in facial anatomy and aesthetics, focusing specifically on the eyes and upper face. We offer a boutique surgical experience with individualized consultations and natural-looking results.

Our practice proudly serves patients from Springboro, Dayton, Cincinnati, Kettering, Centerville, Mason, and surrounding areas. Whether you’re seeking a subtle lift or a comprehensive facial rejuvenation, we’re here to help you look as vibrant as you feel.

What to Expect During the Process

Your surgeon will evaluate your facial features, brow position, and skin elasticity to determine the best surgical approach. Options may include:

  • Endoscopic brow lift (minimally invasive with small incisions)
  • Coronal brow lift (ideal for significant sagging)
  • Temporal or lateral lift (targets the outer brow and eye area)

Recovery typically takes 1–2 weeks, with swelling and bruising gradually subsiding. Most patients return to normal activities quickly and enjoy results that last 10 years or longer.

Reclaim Your Youthful Expression

If your face is sending the wrong message—tired, sad, angry—a brow lift may be the right solution. At AestheticEye in Springboro, we help patients across Cincinnati and Dayton rediscover the brighter, more youthful appearance that reflects how they truly feel inside.

html:
Nov 04, 2025

If you’ve ever felt an uncontrollable twitch or spasm in your eyelid, you’re not alone. Many people experience these involuntary movements, which can range from mildly annoying to seriously disruptive. If your eye twitching is frequent, prolonged, or affecting your quality of life, you may be dealing with blepharospasm—a neurological condition that causes repetitive, uncontrollable contractions of the muscles around the eyes.

At AestheticEye in Cincinnati, OH, our board-certified oculoplastic surgeons, Dr. Henson and Dr. Pargament, specialize in diagnosing and treating blepharospasm. We’re here to help you understand what’s causing your symptoms and offer advanced, personalized treatment options to restore your comfort and peace of mind.

What Is Blepharospasm?

Blepharospasm is a condition characterized by involuntary blinking or eyelid closure caused by abnormal muscle contractions. It usually begins with minor, occasional twitching and can progress over time into more frequent and forceful spasms that interfere with daily activities like reading, driving, or social interactions.

It is classified as a focal dystonia, meaning it involves abnormal nerve signals that cause muscle overactivity in a specific part of the body—in this case, the muscles around the eyes.

Common Causes of Eye Twitching

While occasional eye twitching is common and often harmless, persistent or severe twitching may indicate blepharospasm or another underlying condition. Possible causes include:

  • Fatigue and Stress – Lack of sleep and high stress levels are major contributors to eye muscle spasms.
  • Eye Strain – Excessive screen time, reading, or poor lighting can strain your eye muscles.
  • Dry Eyes – A common issue in adults over 50, dry eyes can trigger spasms as the eye tries to protect itself.
  • Caffeine or Alcohol Use – Both substances can overstimulate your nervous system.
  • Neurological Conditions – Blepharospasm may be linked to conditions like Parkinson’s disease or other dystonias.
  • Medication Side Effects – Certain drugs, especially those affecting the nervous system, can cause muscle twitching.

If your symptoms are ongoing or getting worse, it’s important to seek medical evaluation.

Diagnosis and Evaluation at AestheticEye

At AestheticEye, we take a comprehensive and compassionate approach to diagnosing blepharospasm. During your consultation, Dr. Henson or Dr. Pargament will:

  • Review your medical and symptom history
  • Examine your eyelid function and facial muscles
  • Rule out other causes like dry eye syndrome or hemifacial spasm
  • Discuss how your symptoms are affecting your daily life

We take the time to listen and understand the full scope of your condition so we can develop a treatment plan that works for you.

Blepharospasm Treatment Options

Effective blepharospasm treatment is available—and most patients experience meaningful relief with the right approach. At AestheticEye, we offer advanced options, including:

1. Botulinum Toxin Injections (Botox®)

The most common and effective treatment for blepharospasm. Botox relaxes the overactive muscles, reducing or eliminating spasms for several months at a time. Treatments are quick, minimally invasive, and highly effective—about 90% of patients report symptom improvement.

2. Surgical Treatment (Myectomy)

In more severe or resistant cases, a myectomy may be recommended. This procedure involves surgically removing some of the muscles or nerves causing the spasms. It can provide long-term relief when other treatments fail.

3. Supportive Care

For some patients, managing dry eye, adjusting medications, or reducing screen time can significantly improve symptoms. We can also guide you through lifestyle changes that may help.

Why Choose AestheticEye?

Located in Cincinnati, OH, and serving the Dayton area, AestheticEye is one of the region’s premier oculoplastic practices. Our surgeons, Dr. Henson and Dr. Pargament, bring unmatched experience in treating complex eyelid conditions like blepharospasm. We combine advanced surgical expertise with personalized care to help you feel confident, comfortable, and supported.

We don’t just treat the symptoms—we help you regain your quality of life.

Get the Help You Need

If you’re tired of living with constant eye twitching or muscle spasms, you’re not alone—and you don’t have to suffer in silence. At AestheticEye, we offer effective blepharospasm treatment tailored to your needs and lifestyle. Whether you’re in Cincinnati, Dayton, or the surrounding communities, expert care is just a phone call away.

Contact us today to schedule your consultation and discover how we can help you feel more comfortable in your own skin again.

If your eyes always look tired, heavy, or “sleepy,” even when you feel rested, you’re not imagining it — your upper eyelids may be the reason. As we age, the delicate skin around the eyes begins to stretch, droop, and sag. For some people, genetics or natural facial structure can cause hooding at an even earlier age. This excess skin weighs down the upper eyelids, creating a fatigued or aged expression that doesn’t reflect how you actually feel.

At AestheticEye in Springboro, OH, we specialize in advanced eyelid procedures that rejuvenate the eye area with precision and artistry. One of the most effective solutions for tired, heavy-looking eyes is upper blepharoplasty, also known as an upper eyelid lift. This procedure removes excess skin and tightens the surrounding tissue, restoring a more alert, youthful, and energetic appearance.

Why Upper Eyelids Begin to Sag

A combination of natural changes contributes to “sleepy” eyes:

  • Skin Laxity: The skin around your eyes is the thinnest on your body. Over time, collagen and elastin decrease, causing the skin to lose its elasticity and sag.
  • Fat Redistribution: Aging can cause fat pockets near the upper eyelid to shift or protrude, contributing to a hooded or heavy look.
  • Muscle Weakening: The levator muscle, which lifts the eyelid, can weaken with age or overuse, contributing to drooping.
  • Genetics: Some individuals inherit naturally hooded eyelids or develop eyelid sagging earlier than others.
  • Environmental Factors: Sun exposure, smoking, allergies, and chronic eye rubbing can accelerate eyelid aging.

According to the American Society of Plastic Surgeons, eyelid surgery is one of the top five most popular cosmetic procedures, with thousands of patients choosing upper blepharoplasty each year to refresh and open their eyes.

How Upper Blepharoplasty Rejuvenates Sleepy Eyes

Upper blepharoplasty is a targeted surgical procedure that removes excess skin and may reposition or refine underlying fat. The result is a smoother, firmer eyelid contour that creates a brighter, more lifted appearance. Key benefits include:

  • A More Awake, Energetic Appearance: The upper eyelids play a huge role in facial expression. By reducing heaviness and hooding, the eyes look more open and alert.
  • A Younger-Looking Face: Sagging upper eyelids can add years to your appearance. An eyelid lift provides one of the most noticeable anti-aging improvements with minimal downtime.
  • Improved Symmetry: Upper blepharoplasty can correct uneven eyelids for a more balanced, harmonious look.
  • Better Vision in Some Cases: When excess upper eyelid skin hangs low enough, it can interfere with peripheral vision. Removing this skin can improve sightlines and daily comfort.
  • Natural, Long-Lasting Results: Results typically last 10–15 years, and the surgical incisions are hidden in the natural eyelid crease for a nearly invisible scar.

Who Is a Good Candidate for Upper Blepharoplasty?

You may benefit from this procedure if you notice:

  • Heavy or drooping upper eyelids
  • Hooded eyelids that hide your natural crease
  • Eyes that look tired or sad even when well-rested
  • Makeup smudging due to excess skin
  • Puffiness or loose skin along the upper eyelid

Patients across Cincinnati, Dayton, Springboro, and surrounding communities choose AestheticEye for expert eyelid evaluation and personalized treatment plans.

Why Patients in Cincinnati and Dayton Trust AestheticEye

AestheticEye specializes solely in advanced procedures for the eyes and upper face. This focus allows for exceptional precision, natural outcomes, and personalized care. Patients from the wider Cincinnati and Dayton area seek out our expertise because:

  • We use the latest surgical techniques
  • We prioritize natural-looking results
  • We provide compassionate, thorough consultations
  • We tailor each procedure to your unique eyelid anatomy and goals

Your eyes are the focal point of your face — they deserve expert attention.

A recent Wall Street Journal article explored why cosmetic eyelid surgery, or blepharoplasty, is becoming more popular. At AestheticEye, we’ve seen the same trend and know that this procedure can do more than just lift your eyelids. It can increase confidence and improve the way you experience daily life! In this post, we will walk you through what a blepharoplasty is, why more young people are choosing it, and how to schedule your appointment with one of our surgeons.

What is a Blepharoplasty?

If you’re tired of dealing with heavy eyelids that make you look tired or even affect your vision, a blepharoplasty could be the answer for you! This procedure removes extra skin, muscle, and sometimes fat from the eyelids giving them a smoother, lifted look. At AestheticEye, our surgeons use advanced techniques to make sure you get natural looking results. During the procedure, our surgeons will create a small incision along the natural crease of your eyelid, allowing them to remove or reposition what’s needed. The incision is then closed, leaving a well-hidden scar that blends into the natural eyelid fold.

Why Younger Adults Are Turning to Eyelid Surgery

It’s not just older adults asking about eyelid surgery anymore. With Zoom meetings, selfies, and social media being part of daily life, it’s hard not to notice the little things. The Wall Street Journal article highlights just how much our screen-filled world may be influencing this trend. According to the article, American Society of Plastic Surgeons (ASPS) president Dr. Bob Basu credits the rise in blepharoplasty to the amount of time people spend seeing themselves on video, stating, “Constant self-viewing makes eyelid heaviness and a chronically tired appearance far more noticeable.”

Beyond just noticing it more, screen time may also be playing a physical role. Dr. Jennifer Tsai, a Manhattan optometrist, explains, “Constant squinting, reduced blinking and rubbing the eyes due to eyestrain can accelerate laxity and puffiness.” When you think about how many hours most of us spend looking at phones and computers each day, it makes sense that the eye area would start to show it.

There’s also another factor doctors are seeing more often: rapid weight loss. Dr. Robert Schwarcz, who founded a Manhattan oculofacial plastic surgery practice, has observed changes connected to the growing use of GLP-1 medications. “A lot of patients are on GLP-1s nowadays and when the midface drops there’s less support for the lower eyelid too and bags become more obvious,” he explained. As faces change with weight loss, the eye area can look more hollow or tired, pushing some patients to explore surgical options sooner than they might have in the past.

Take the Next Step

You can also call (937) 800-4957 or text (937) 918-7631 to schedule a consultation or ask any questions you may have!

html:
Apr 07, 2026

Hypothyroidism is a common endocrine disorder that affects millions of people, particularly women, in the United States. Characterized by an underactive thyroid gland, hypothyroidism can lead to a variety of symptoms, including fatigue, weight gain and cold intolerance.

However, many people are unaware that hypothyroidism can also have significant effects on the eyes. In particular, hypothyroidism is often associated with a condition called Thyroid Eye Disease (TED), an autoimmune disorder that can impact your vision and appearance.

What is Thyroid Eye Disease?

Thyroid Eye Disease, also known as Graves’ Ophthalmopathy or Graves’ Orbitopathy, is an autoimmune condition most commonly linked with hyperthyroidism (overactive thyroid), but it can also occur with hypothyroidism or even in people with normal thyroid function. In TED, the body’s immune system mistakenly attacks the tissues and muscles around the eyes. This causes inflammation, swelling and tissue remodeling, which can result in a range of symptoms affecting both the function and appearance of the eyes.

Symptoms of Thyroid Eye Disease

  • Bulging or protruding eyes (proptosis)
  • Redness and swelling of the eyelids
  • Dry, gritty, or irritated eyes
  • Double vision (diplopia)
  • Difficulty closing the eyes completely
  • Eye pain or pressure
  • Light sensitivity

Left untreated, TED can lead to serious complications, including vision loss. Early diagnosis and appropriate treatment are essential to managing the condition and preserving eye health.

How Can Oculoplastic and Orbital Surgery Help?

At AestheticEye, serving Cincinnati and Dayton, OH, our board-certified oculoplastic surgeons are uniquely equipped to diagnose and treat Thyroid Eye Disease. While mild cases can often be managed with medications, artificial tears and lifestyle modifications, moderate-to-severe TED may require surgical intervention to restore both function and appearance.

Oculoplastic and orbital surgeries for TED may include:

  • Orbital decompression surgery: Removes bone or fat from behind the eye to relieve pressure and reduce bulging.
  • Eyelid surgery: Corrects eyelid retraction, improves eyelid closure and enhances appearance.
  • Strabismus surgery: Addresses double vision by realigning the eye muscles.

These procedures are highly specialized and require the expertise of an oculoplastic surgeon with experience in the delicate anatomy of the eyelids and orbit.

Thyroid Eye Disease FAQs

1. Can hypothyroidism really cause eye problems?
Yes. While TED is more often linked to hyperthyroidism, it can also occur in people with hypothyroidism, especially those with autoimmune thyroid disease (Hashimoto’s thyroiditis).

2. Will treating my thyroid condition cure my eye symptoms?
Managing your thyroid hormone levels is important, but TED can progress independently of thyroid control. Ongoing eye care and monitoring are essential.

3. What are the first signs of Thyroid Eye Disease?
Early signs include redness, swelling and a sensation of grittiness in the eyes. Bulging eyes and double vision often appear later.

4. Is surgery always necessary for TED?
No. Mild cases may be managed with medications, lifestyle changes and regular eye care. Surgery is reserved for more severe cases that affect vision or cause significant discomfort.

5. How do I know if I need to see an oculoplastic surgeon?
If you have thyroid disease and notice any changes in your eyes—such as bulging, double vision or difficulty closing your eyes—schedule a consultation with an oculoplastic specialist for a comprehensive evaluation.

html:
Jun 09, 2026

Watery eyes can be more than a minor annoyance when they keep coming back. Constant tearing can blur your vision, run down your cheeks, irritate the skin around your eyes, or make it look like you’re crying when you aren’t. The cause isn’t always obvious, either. Sometimes the eye is making too many tears. Other times, tears can’t drain the way they should.

Why Do My Eyes Keep Watering?

Excessive tearing, also called epiphora, can happen when your eyes overproduce tears or when the tear drainage system isn’t working correctly. Dry eye, allergies, eyelid inflammation, corneal irritation, eyelid position changes, narrowed tear drainage openings, and blocked tear ducts can all play a role. That’s why a focused eye exam matters before assuming you need a specific procedure.

Can Dry Eye Cause Watery Eyes?

Yes. Dry eye can sometimes trigger reflex tearing. When the eye surface gets irritated, your body may respond by producing extra tears, even though those tears may not fix the underlying dryness. If your eyes feel watery, gritty, burning, or tired, the source of the tearing may start at the eye surface instead of the tear duct.

When Tearing Is a Drainage Problem

Your tears normally drain through tiny openings near the inner corners of your eyelids. These openings lead into a drainage system that carries tears toward the nose. If one part of that system narrows or becomes blocked, tears may overflow onto the eyelid or cheek.

At AestheticEye, our board-certified oculoplastic surgeons evaluate excessive tearing to find where the problem starts. If the punctum, the small drainage opening in the eyelid, is narrowed or blocked, punctoplasty may help widen that opening. If the blockage is deeper in the nasolacrimal duct, DCR surgery may be discussed.

What Is DCR Surgery?

Dacryocystorhinostomy, usually called DCR surgery, creates a new pathway for tears to drain into the nose. This procedure bypasses a blocked nasolacrimal duct so tears can move through a new drainage route. AestheticEye offers traditional external DCR and endoscopic DCR, depending on the patient’s anatomy and needs. In some cases, a small stent may be placed during healing to help keep the new pathway open.

Why See an Oculoplastic Surgeon for Chronic Tearing?

Tearing problems can involve the eyelids, tear ducts, eye surface, and nearby facial anatomy. That makes oculoplastic training especially relevant. Dr. Ginger Henson and Dr. Jonathan Pargament are board-certified oculoplastic surgeons serving patients from Springboro, Cincinnati, and Dayton. They can evaluate whether your tearing is related to irritation, eyelid position, punctal narrowing, a blocked tear duct, or another concern.

title: Is Your Eyelid Turning In or Out? What to Know About Eyelid Malposition
description: If your eyelid turns inward, pulls away from your eye, or makes it feel like your lashes are rubbing the surface, eyelid malposition may be part of the

headings.title: What Is the Difference Between Entropion and Ectropion?
What Causes an Eyelid to Turn In or Out?

html:
Jul 10, 2026

If your eyelid turns inward, pulls away from your eye, or makes it feel like your lashes are rubbing the surface, eyelid malposition may be part of the problem. Because the eyelids help protect the eye and guide tear movement, changes in eyelid position deserve a focused exam.

What Is Eyelid Malposition?

Eyelid malposition means the eyelid isn’t sitting in proper alignment. At AestheticEye, our board-certified oculoplastic surgeons treat eyelid malposition repair when it affects comfort, eye protection, tear movement, or appearance. The condition can involve the upper or lower eyelid, but two common lower-lid problems are entropion and ectropion. Symptoms may include redness, tearing, irritation, discharge, light sensitivity, or a gritty feeling.

What Is the Difference Between Entropion and Ectropion?

Entropion and ectropion change how the eyelid rests against the eye, but they move in opposite directions:

  • Entropion: The eyelid turns inward, which may cause the lashes or lid margin to rub against the eye.
  • Ectropion: The eyelid turns outward or pulls away from the eye, which may expose the inner eyelid and eye surface.

The NCBI Bookshelf StatPearls entry on ectropion notes that outward turning of the eyelid can contribute to dryness, redness, tearing, and foreign body sensation because the eye surface isn’t protected normally.

Why Does Eyelid Position Matter?

Your eyelids spread tears across the eye, protect the cornea, and help the eye close comfortably. When the eyelid turns inward, the lashes may scrape the cornea or conjunctiva. When it turns outward, the eye may stay exposed and irritated. StatPearls also explains that entropion can rotate the eyelid margin and lashes toward the eye, which may irritate or injure the cornea or conjunctiva over time.

What Causes an Eyelid to Turn In or Out?

Eyelid malposition can develop from age-related eyelid laxity, scarring, trauma, facial paralysis, inflammation, congenital factors, or changes after prior surgery. Tearing, redness, irritation, and gritty eyes can also come from dry eye, allergies, infection, or other eyelid conditions, so an exam is the first step.

When Should You See an Oculoplastic Surgeon?

Consider an evaluation if your eyelid turns inward or outward, your lashes rub your eye, tearing keeps recurring, or redness and irritation don’t settle. A general eye exam can identify many common causes of irritation. When the eyelid itself is turning in or out, repair planning often calls for an oculofacial plastic surgeon who works with eyelid architecture around the eye.

At AestheticEye in Springboro, Dr. Ginger Henson and Dr. Jonathan Pargament evaluate eyelid position concerns for patients along the Cincinnati-Dayton I-75 corridor. During an exam, we can check eyelid position, eyelid laxity, tear movement, and whether the eye surface shows irritation. Dr. Pargament has oculofacial plastic and reconstructive surgery training, board certification, and academic experience in oculoplastic surgery.

FAQ About Eyelid Malposition

Can eyelid malposition cause watery eyes?

Yes. Poor eyelid position can affect tear movement or irritate the eye surface, which may trigger tearing.

Is entropion the same as ectropion?

No. Entropion turns inward. Ectropion turns outward.

Does eyelid malposition always need surgery?

No. Treatment depends on the cause, severity, symptoms, and exam findings.

Can eyelid malposition affect vision?

It can blur vision if tearing, irritation, or corneal exposure affects the eye surface.

The Role of Blepharoplasty

Blepharoplasty, or eyelid surgery, is an effective solution for men looking to refresh their appearance. The procedure involves the removal of excess skin, muscle and fat from the eyelids, resulting in a more awake and youthful look. At AestheticEye in Cincinnati, OH, our board-certified oculoplastic surgeons, Dr. Ginger Henson and Dr. Jonathan Pargament, specialize in this procedure and understand the unique needs of male patients.

One of the most appealing aspects of blepharoplasty is its ability to create subtle, natural-looking results that enhance one’s features without being overly dramatic. Many men fear that cosmetic surgery will make them look artificial or overly “done.” However, with the expertise of our surgeons, the goal is to achieve a refreshed appearance that looks both natural and appropriate for any workplace setting.

A Rejuvenated Look Can Boost Confidence and Opportunities

Undergoing blepharoplasty can lead to psychological benefits, including increased self-confidence and higher self-esteem. A study in the July 2024 Healthcare Journal shows that individuals who feel good about their appearance are more likely to engage positively in social interactions, which can, in turn, enhance their work relationships. Increased confidence can actively shape how individuals present themselves in interviews and meetings, leading to improved career outcomes.

Additionally, many organizations readily admit that they take appearance into account during the recruitment process. By addressing concerns related to one’s appearance through procedures like blepharoplasty, men may find themselves better positioned for career advancements.

html:
Aug 11, 2026

Revision eyelid surgery may be worth considering when problems from a previous eyelid procedure remain after healing or interfere with eye comfort, closure, vision, or appearance. A second operation isn’t automatically the answer. The first step is an exam that separates temporary healing changes from concerns that may benefit from correction.

What Can Revision Eyelid Surgery Address?

Also called secondary eyelid surgery or revision blepharoplasty, this procedure is tailored to the result of the first operation. At AestheticEye, revision planning may address:

  • asymmetry or visible scarring
  • persistent puffiness or drooping
  • a hollow or tight appearance
  • eyelid retraction or difficulty closing the eye

Each of these concerns calls for a different approach. If you have extra skin left, you’ll need a different plan than someone whose eyelid sits too low or whose eye surface is exposed.

Why Is a Second Eyelid Procedure More Complex?

Once you’ve had eyelid surgery, the tissue around your eyes isn’t quite the same. Scar tissue, changes in fat, and shifts in eyelid support can make things less predictable. A peer-reviewed review of cosmetic eyelid surgery complications describes functional and cosmetic problems that may call for careful management after blepharoplasty.

Research on eyelid malposition after blepharoplasty also emphasizes the need to evaluate eyelid support and eye-surface risk. A revision consultation should look beyond symmetry and consider blinking, closure, tear distribution, and corneal protection.

How Soon Can You Have Revision Blepharoplasty?

How soon you can have revision blepharoplasty depends on what’s going on with your eyelids. Swelling and scar tissue can continue to change for months, so your surgeon may suggest waiting until things settle before making any decisions. If you’re having trouble closing your eyes, dealing with pain, or noticing vision changes, it’s important to get checked sooner, even if you don’t need another surgery right away.

Why Choose an Oculoplastic Surgeon for Revision Eyelid Surgery?

Revision work involves appearance and eye function. AestheticEye’s board-certified oculoplastic surgeons, Dr. Ginger Henson and Dr. Jonathan Pargament, have specialized training in ophthalmology and oculofacial plastic and reconstructive surgery.

With offices in Cincinnati and Springboro, AestheticEye gives patients along the I-75 corridor access to surgeons whose work centers on eyelids, tear drainage, and structures around the eye. During a consultation, the team can review your prior surgery, examine eyelid position and closure, and explain what correction may realistically accomplish.

FAQ About Revision Eyelid Surgery

Does an uneven result always require another surgery?
No. Healing, swelling, and preexisting facial asymmetry can affect how the eyelids look. An exam can clarify whether more time or treatment is appropriate.

Can revision surgery remove all visible scarring?
No procedure can promise scar-free skin. A revision may improve certain scars, depending on their location and the available tissue.

Is revision surgery only cosmetic?
No. It may also address functional problems such as poor eyelid closure, retraction, irritation, or interference with vision.

Will insurance cover a revision?
Coverage varies. Functional correction may qualify in some cases, while cosmetic revision usually doesn’t.

Aging is inevitable, but the signs of aging around your eyes don’t have to be. At AestheticEye in Dayton, OH, we offer a range of non-surgical treatments to help you rejuvenate and revitalize your eyes without the need for surgery. Here’s a closer look at the non-surgical options available to reverse aging eyes and help you achieve a refreshed, youthful appearance.

Understanding Non-Surgical Eye Rejuvenation

Non-surgical eye rejuvenation involves minimally invasive treatments designed to address common signs of aging such as wrinkles, fine lines, dark circles, and puffiness. These treatments offer a more subtle and natural-looking result compared to surgical options, with minimal downtime and quick recovery.

Our Top Non-Surgical Treatments

BOTOX®
BOTOX® is a trusted treatment for reducing the appearance of dynamic wrinkles caused by facial expressions. It’s particularly effective for treating crow’s feet and frown lines between the eyebrows. BOTOX® works by temporarily relaxing the muscles that cause wrinkles, resulting in smoother skin and a more relaxed appearance.
Chemical Peels
Chemical peels are an excellent option for improving the texture and tone of the skin around your eyes. They help reduce fine lines, wrinkles, and pigmentation issues, revealing fresher, younger-looking skin. Our team at AestheticEye tailors chemical peels to your specific skin type and concerns, ensuring optimal results.
Laser Treatments
Laser treatments can effectively target and reduce dark circles, pigmentation, and fine lines around the eyes. These treatments stimulate collagen production, which helps improve skin elasticity and firmness. Laser treatments are precise and can be customized to address your unique needs.
Skin Care Products
In addition to in-office treatments, we offer medical-grade skin care products that can enhance and maintain the results of your non-surgical procedures. These products are specially formulated to target the delicate skin around the eyes, providing hydration, protection, and rejuvenation.

Benefits of Non-Surgical Eye Rejuvenation

Choosing non-surgical treatments for eye rejuvenation offers several benefits:

  • Minimal Downtime: Non-surgical treatments typically require little to no downtime, allowing you to resume your normal activities quickly.
  • Natural-Looking Results: These treatments enhance your natural beauty without the drastic changes that surgery can sometimes bring. You’ll look refreshed and youthful without appearing overdone.
  • Quick Results: Many non-surgical treatments provide immediate or fast results, so you can enjoy the benefits soon after your appointment.
  • Customizable: Non-surgical treatments can be tailored to your specific concerns and desired outcomes, ensuring you get the best possible results.

Patient-Centered Care at AestheticEye

Our experienced oculoplastic surgeons, Dr. Ginger Henson and Dr. Jonathan Pargament, will work closely with you to develop a personalized treatment plan that addresses your unique needs and concerns.

html:
Sep 15, 2026

Most eyelid bumps aren’t serious, but if you notice a lump that keeps coming back, changes, bleeds, affects your lashes, or makes it harder to move your eyelid, it’s time to get it checked. You can’t always tell what an eyelid lesion is just by looking, and similar-looking bumps can need very different care.

What Can Cause an Eyelid Bump?

An eyelid lesion can develop from a blocked gland, infection, cyst, skin growth, or tumor. A clinical review of benign eyelid lesions in NCBI Bookshelf lists common possibilities such as chalazia, papillomas, inclusion cysts, and other noncancerous growths.

Most lesions aren’t harmful. Where the bump is, how it’s growing, and your symptoms help decide if you need to watch it, treat it, remove it, or get a biopsy.

Which Eyelid Changes Should You Get Checked?

Plan to schedule an eyelid lesion evaluation if you notice any of these changes:

  • growth or a change in shape, size, or color
  • bleeding, crusting, an open sore, or a spot that won’t heal
  • missing eyelashes or distortion of the eyelid margin
  • a lump that keeps coming back in the same spot or makes it harder to blink or see

These signs don’t prove that a lesion is cancerous. A clinical review of malignant eyelid lesions explains that clinicians consider a growth’s timeline, rate of change, bleeding, lash loss, and recurrence when deciding whether biopsy is appropriate. Sudden vision changes, severe pain, fever, or rapidly spreading swelling need prompt medical care.

What Happens During an Eyelid Lesion Evaluation?

During your evaluation, the provider will check where the lesion is, what it looks like, how deep it goes, how it’s changed over time, and how it affects your eyelid. They’ll also look at your lashes, eyelid edge, eye surface, and the tissue around it.

When the diagnosis isn’t clear from the exam, a biopsy may be recommended. Depending on the lesion and its location, AestheticEye’s eyelid lesion removal services may include biopsy, removal, and reconstruction planning to preserve eyelid function and healthy tissue.

Why Does Oculoplastic Training Matter for Eyelid Lesion Removal?

Your eyelids are thin and flexible, protecting your eyes and helping you blink and move tears. If you need a growth removed near your lash line or eyelid edge, it takes careful work to protect healthy tissue and plan for reconstruction if needed.

Dr. Ginger Henson and Dr. Jonathan Pargament have completed advanced training in ophthalmology and oculofacial plastic and reconstructive surgery. If you’re in the Cincinnati-Dayton I-75 area, you can visit AestheticEye’s Cincinnati or Springboro offices to see specialists who look at both the lesion and the eyelid structure around it.

FAQ About Eyelid Bumps and Lesions

Is every eyelid lesion cancerous?
No. Most are benign, but you’ll need an exam to know for sure what your bump is.

Can a chalazion look like another eyelid lesion?
Yes. If you have a bump that keeps coming back or looks unusual, it’s a good idea to get it checked instead of trying home treatments over and over.

Does every eyelid bump need removal?
No. Treatment depends on what the bump is, your symptoms, where it is, and if it’s changing.

Will eyelid lesion removal leave a scar?
Any procedure can leave a scar, but how visible it is depends on the lesion, where it is, how it’s removed, how you heal, and if reconstruction is needed.

description: A bulging eye, new double vision, eye-socket pressure, or unexplained vision changes can be orbital tumor symptoms, but they can also result from thyroid

headings.title: What Are Common Orbital Tumor Symptoms?

What Happens During an Orbital Tumor Evaluation?
When Is Orbital Tumor Surgery Considered?
Why See an Oculoplastic Surgeon for an Orbital Problem?
Schedule an Orbital Tumor Evaluation in Cincinnati or Springboro

html:
Oct 01, 2026

A bulging eye, new double vision, eye-socket pressure, or unexplained vision changes can be orbital tumor symptoms, but they can also result from thyroid eye disease, inflammation, infection, vascular disorders, and other conditions. An exam can help identify the cause without assuming a tumor is responsible.

What Are Common Orbital Tumor Symptoms?

The orbit is the bony socket containing the eye, muscles, nerves, blood vessels, fat, and other tissues. Because these structures share a confined space, an orbital mass can affect nearby eye function.

A 2026 NCBI clinical review of benign orbital tumors notes that possible signs and symptoms include:

  • a bulging eye, also called proptosis
  • double vision or restricted eye movement
  • eye or orbital pain
  • decreased or blurred vision
  • eyelid changes, including drooping

Some orbital tumors cause few or no symptoms at first. Symptoms vary with the mass’s location and effect on nearby structures.

Does a Bulging Eye Always Mean There Is a Tumor?

No. Proptosis and other orbital symptoms can have non-tumor causes. The same NCBI review includes thyroid eye disease, inflammatory disorders, and infections among conditions that can resemble an orbital mass.

Appearance alone can’t confirm the cause; changes in eye position, movement, or vision need an exam to determine what is happening inside the orbit.

What Happens During an Orbital Tumor Evaluation?

An orbital tumor evaluation may include checks of vision, pupils, eye movement, and how far the eye projects forward. Imaging often plays an important role when a mass is suspected.

The Oculofacial Society’s orbital tumor guidance explains that CT or MRI may be used to locate and evaluate a tumor, and some cases require biopsy. Some benign tumors can be observed, so finding a mass doesn’t automatically mean surgery is needed.

When Is Orbital Tumor Surgery Considered?

Treatment depends on the diagnosis, symptoms, location, and effect on surrounding structures. Tumors affecting vision, eye movement, or eye position may be considered for surgery, while some lesions can be monitored or treated another way.

AestheticEye provides evaluation and orbital tumor surgery in southwest Ohio. Depending on the diagnosis and location, care may also involve other specialists.

Why See an Oculoplastic Surgeon for an Orbital Problem?

Orbital care involves both eye function and the anatomy surrounding the eye. Dr. Ginger Henson and Dr. Jonathan Pargament both completed ophthalmology residency and fellowship training in ophthalmic or oculofacial plastic and reconstructive surgery.

With offices in Cincinnati and Springboro, AestheticEye gives patients along the Cincinnati-Dayton corridor access to specialists focused on the eyelids, orbit, and surrounding structures.

FAQ About Orbital Tumor Symptoms

Are all orbital tumors cancerous?
No. Orbital tumors can be benign or malignant, and evaluation is needed to determine the type of mass.

Can an orbital tumor cause double vision?
Yes. A mass can affect or restrict eye movement, which may lead to double vision.

Does an orbital tumor always require surgery?
No. Treatment depends on the diagnosis, symptoms, location, and effect on nearby structures.

title: Meet the Team
html:
Dr. Ginger Henson

Dr. Ginger Henson, M.D. is a board certified oculofacial plastic surgeon serving the Cincinnati/Dayton area. Born and raised in Cincinnati, Dr. Henson is a graduate of Miami University and earned her medical degree from the University of Cincinnati College of Medicine. She then completed her Ophthalmology residency at the prestigious Bascom Palmer Eye Institute in Miami, Florida. During her residency, Dr. Henson developed a deep appreciation for the artistry of oculofacial plastic surgery. She returned to Cincinnati to master the nuances of oculofacial plastic surgery during her fellowship in Ophthalmic Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery at the Cincinnati Eye Institute. Throughout her career, she has served in many capacities including Director of Pediatric Oculoplastic Surgery at Cincinnati Children’s Hospital Medical Center and Director of Oculoplastic Surgery at the University of Cincinnati. In addition, she served on the Board of Directors at the Cincinnati Eye Institute for many years.

After practicing for over 15 years, Dr. Henson co-founded her own private practice along with her colleague, Dr. Jonathan Pargament. Their vision for AestheticEye Oculoplastic Surgeons is to deliver outstanding surgical results with an exceptional patient experience in a supportive, relaxed environment. She continues to teach and mentor resident surgeons and medical students as a volunteer Professor of Ophthalmology at the University of Cincinnati.

Dr. Henson was awarded a Top Doctor award from Castle Connolly. The Castle Connolly recognition in medicine is considered by physicians to be the only legitimate recognized category of excellence in American Medicine.

Dr. Henson is skilled in cosmetic upper and lower eyelid surgery, brow surgery, and MOHS reconstructive surgery. She also has a passion for non-surgical facial rejuvenation techniques including neurotoxins, CO2 laser resurfacing and IPL.In her free time, she enjoys traveling with her husband and keeping up with their five children and spoiled goldendoodle, Paxton.

Dr. Jonathan Pargament

Jonathan Pargament, M.D. is an experienced oculofacial plastic surgeon in the Cincinnati/Dayton area and co-founder of AestheticEye Oculoplastic Surgeons. Born and raised in Toledo, he holds an honors degree from the University of Michigan and earned his medical degree from the University of Cincinnati. He completed his ophthalmology residency at the University of Cincinnati before completing in a rigorous three-year oculofacial plastic and reconstructive surgery fellowship at the Center for Facial Appearances in Salt Lake City. Dr. Pargament then spent the next 8 years after fellowship growing a successful oculoplastic practice in the Cincinnati/Dayton area as partner in a large multi-speciality ophthalmology group in the region.

In 2025, Dr. Pargament and Dr. Henson decided to start their own practice, AestheticEye Oculoplastic Surgeons, to continue serving the needs of their patients in the Dayton and Cincinnati area. Dr. Pargament’s particular interests include endoscopic and minimally invasive brow lifts, upper and lower lid rejuvenation procedures and reconstructive surgeries after skin cancer removal (Mohs). He is a board-certified member of the American Academy of Ophthalmology and American Society of Oculoplastic and Reconstructive Surgeons. He is an adjunct professor of plastic surgery and ophthalmology and director of oculoplastic and reconstructive surgery at the University of Cincinnati. Dr. Pargament has delivered numerous presentations at regional and national meetings and authored many book chapters and peer-reviewed journal articles.

Today, Dr. Pargament co-leads AestheticEye Oculoplastic Surgeons, mentors aspiring surgeons and dedicates his expertise to the underserved at the University of Cincinnati Hoxworth Eye Clinic. Outside of work, Dr. Pargament stays busy with his three young children and rescue lab, Sadie, that he shares with his wife and neuro-ophthalmologist, Dr. Laura Hanson. He loves the outdoors, especially fly-fishing, and international travel.

Sarah Morris

Sarah Morris, APRN, FNP-C is a board-certified Family Nurse Practitioner with specialized expertise in oculoplastic care. Originally from Flemingsburg, Kentucky, Sarah earned her Bachelor of Science in Exercise Science from the University of Kentucky before pursuing her Bachelor of Science in Nursing at Bellarmine University in Louisville, Kentucky.

Following completion of her nursing degree, Sarah practiced in the Cardiovascular Intensive Care Unit at University of Kentucky Hospital, where she developed a strong clinical foundation caring for complex medical and surgical patients. She later earned her Family Nurse Practitioner degree from the University of South Florida in Tampa, graduating with honors and earning induction into the Sigma Theta Tau International Honor Society of Nursing. She is an active member of the American Association of Nurse Practitioners.

At AestheticEye, Sarah works closely with Dr. Ginger Henson and Dr. Jon Pargament to provide comprehensive perioperative and non-surgical care. She manages post-operative patients, performs in-office procedures such as biopsies of suspicious lesions and chalazion treatments when clinically indicated, and offers aesthetic services including neurotoxin treatments with Dysport® and Botox® as well as UltraClear® laser treatments.

Outside of the office, Sarah enjoys staying active, spending time outdoors, and attending sporting events—especially cheering on the Kentucky Wildcats. She also values time traveling and making memories with her husband, Nat, and their two daughters.

Renee Ingle

With more than 30 years of experience in advanced skincare, Renee is a trusted and familiar face in the field of aesthetic care. Her approach combines deep clinical knowledge with a warm, patient-centered touch—making every treatment both effective and comfortable.

At AestheticEye, Renee provides a full range of customized skincare services, including HydraFacial®, chemical peels, microneedling, and dermaplaning, as well as personalized treatment plans tailored to each patient’s skin goals. She believes that beautiful skin begins with a healthy foundation and focuses on treatments that restore balance, radiance, and confidence.

Renee’s passion for skincare is matched only by her dedication to patient relationships. She takes pride in creating a welcoming experience where patients feel understood, supported, and genuinely cared for. Her decades of experience allow her to deliver consistent, natural-looking results that align perfectly with AestheticEye’s commitment to excellence and patient-centered care.
